articles.title: Aaron Rodgers bought a $28 million Malibu mansion in 2019, 7 years later, the NFL legend is seeking $39.5 million
articles.summary: NFL News: Aaron Rodgers is putting a spectacular slice of Malibu coastline up for sale, and the asking price is turning heads. The NFL quarterback paid $28 mill.
articles.body: Aaron Rodgers is putting a spectacular slice of Malibu coastline up for sale, and the asking price is turning heads. The NFL quarterback paid $28 million for the oceanfront estate in 2019. Now, seven years later, he wants $39.5 million for the property. The listing marks another major move in Rodgers' real estate portfolio as he approaches the final chapter of his football career. Beyond the eye-catching price, the mansion's private beach access, sweeping Pacific views and celebrity ownership history make it a standout in California's luxury property market.Aaron Rodgers lists his Malibu mansion for $39.5 millionRodgers' Malibu estate hit the market in August 2026 with an asking price of $39.5 million, according to Realtor.com. The Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback bought the property in 2019 for $28 million, during his time with the Green Bay Packers and relationship with former racing driver Danica Patrick.The difference between the purchase price and the current asking price is $11.5 million. If the home sells at the listed amount, that would represent an increase of roughly 41% before accounting for renovation costs, taxes, upkeep and selling expenses.The listing is notable not just for its price, but also for its timing. Rodgers has been putting several properties on the market as he prepares for what has been described as his final NFL season. His Malibu home is the most expensive of the three properties reportedly listed, placing it at the centre of his real estate reshuffle.The property is being marketed for its location and features rather than its famous owner. The listing highlights the estate's oceanfront setting, direct beach access and refined coastal design.Inside Aaron Rodgers' luxurious Malibu beachfront estateRodgers' Malibu property is less a conventional mansion and more a private coastal compound. The estate includes a three-story main residence and a separate two-bedroom guesthouse, offering space for visitors while maintaining privacy in the primary home.The main house features four bedrooms and four bathrooms, with expansive windows that frame the Pacific Ocean. Its design blends indoor and outdoor living, allowing natural light and ocean views to shape the feel of the interiors.The grounds add to the home's resort-like appeal. A swimming pool, outdoor lounge areas and landscaped spaces create places to relax while taking in the coastline. The estate also includes a private funicular, a hillside transport system that provides access down toward the beach.That combination of privacy, architecture and direct connection to the ocean helps explain why the home commands a premium price. Malibu's beachfront properties are limited by geography, and estates with expansive views and beach access occupy a distinctive place in the luxury market.The home's separate guesthouse also gives it flexibility for entertaining or hosting family and friends. Rather than relying solely on square footage, the property offers a collection of spaces designed around the setting.From Robbie Williams to Aaron Rodgers: The mansion's celebrity historyThe Malibu estate had a notable list of owners before Rodgers took possession. British singer Robbie Williams and his wife, Ayda Field, sold the property to Rodgers and Patrick after reportedly purchasing it for $20.25 million in 2018.Before Williams, the home was associated with Netflix executive Ted Sarandos and his wife, Nicole Avant. The property's history adds another layer of appeal for buyers interested in high-profile real estate.Rodgers and Patrick reportedly rented the home before completing the purchase. The transaction closed in November 2019, with the $28 million deal widely reported at the time. The purchase placed Rodgers among the high-profile athletes investing in California's luxury coastal market.The mansion also drew attention in January 2025, when devastating wildfires affected parts of Southern California. Rodgers said his home was not damaged, though people close to him lost theirs."My home is fine. I’m not in the areas that have been affected, but it’s been a weird time for so many that live down here," he said during an appearance on "The Pat McAfee Show.""Friends of mine have lost houses. A number of friends in Palisades have lost their homes, a number of friends in Pasadena were affected, friends around Runyon Canyon."His comments highlighted the wider impact of the fires on communities across the region, even as his own property remained safe.Aaron Rodgers' Malibu listing comes amid a wider real estate sell-offThe $39.5 million Malibu listing is part of a broader property shake-up for Rodgers. The quarterback has also reportedly listed homes in New Jersey and Wisconsin, bringing the combined asking price of the three properties to approximately $58.2 million.His New Jersey mansion, which he purchased for $9.5 million in 2023 after joining the New York Jets, has reportedly been listed for $15 million. Meanwhile, his Wisconsin property, bought in 2015 for just over $1.7 million, has an asking price of $3.7 million.Together, the listings point to a major shift in Rodgers' real estate holdings. Still, listing prices do not guarantee final sale prices, and the difference between what he paid and what he is asking should not be viewed as confirmed profit. Renovations, property taxes, insurance, maintenance and transaction costs can all affect the final return.The Malibu mansion remains the headline property in the group. Its oceanfront location, guesthouse and private beach access distinguish it from the other homes, while its $39.5 million price tag places it in a rarefied segment of the market.Whether Rodgers secures the full asking price remains to be seen. articles.title: Sam Darnold Injury Update, Latest Rumors on Seahawks QB's Return Timeline Amid Glute Issue
articles.summary: Seattle Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold has "a chance" to return from his glute injury on Sunday against the Washington Commanders and will return to practice this week, per NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.
articles.body:
Seattle Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold has "a chance" to return from his glute injury on Sunday against the Washington Commanders and will return to practice this week, per NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.

Rapoport added that the Seahawks are going to be "cautious" with Darnold's return and there could "maybe be another week of Drew Lock, but sooner rather than later for Darnold."

The plan has been to get Darnold back on the practice field Wednesday.

"Right now, the plan is for him to be out there in some capacity, and we'll go from there," head coach Mike Macdonald told reporters on Monday. "How much, we'll see from here to Wednesday on what that number is. But right now, that's the goal."

Darnold suffered the injury just five plays into the season-opening win over the New England Patriots. He was replaced by Lock, who has been fantastic in relief duty, throwing for 422 yards, four touchdowns and no interceptions while completing 72.9 percent of his passes in parts of two games.

The 29-year-old Darnold led Seattle to a Super Bowl title last season, throwing for 4,048 yards, 25 touchdowns and 14 interceptions during the regular season and 672 yards, five scores and zero interceptions in the playoffs. It was quite the debut season in Seattle.

And the Seahawks have little reason to rush him back given Lock's strong play and the 2-0 start. Nonetheless, it sounds like Darnold will return to action in the next week or two.

articles.title: Packers WR Jayden Reed 'doing OK,' but 'too early' to tell if he'll play again this season; RT Zach Bako-Bewele out for season with knee injury
articles.summary: Reed is back in Green Bay and undergoing further testing with doctors.
articles.body:
The Green Bay Packers provided significant updates on Tuesday regarding two of their key injured offensive starters.

Starting right tackle Zach Bako-Bewele confirmed that he's out for the season with a torn patellar tendon in his right knee. And head coach Matt LaFleur told reporters that "it's too early" to tell if wide receiver Jayden Reed will be able to return this season from a neck injury.

Reed left Sunday's win over the New York Jets with the neck injury that required an overnight stay in New Jersey . He took direct contact to the crown of his helmet on a tackle that left him lying on his back after the hit. The Packers announced that he had movement in his extremities, but he did not travel back with the team Sunday night for medical-observation purposes.

Reed is back in Green Bay as of Tuesday, and LaFleur confirmed it was a neck injury amid conflicting reports that he'd sustained a back injury. LaFleur told reporters that he thinks Reed is "doing OK." But as of now, Reed's status moving forward and for the rest of the season is unclear.

"He's back in Green Bay and, obviously, still going through a lot of testing and consulting with doctors," LaFleur said of Reed. "From what I'm told, he's doing OK."

LaFleur was then asked about Reed's status for the rest of the season.

"It's way too early for that right now," LaFleur said. "He's just got a lot — there's a lot going on."

The precise nature of Reed's injury is unclear.

Bako-Bewele needs surgery; his season is over

Bako-Bewele's status is clear. He told reporters at his locker Tuesday that he'd suffered a complete tear of the patellar tendon in his right knee and needs surgery. The injury is to the same tendon that sustained a partial tear in Week 15 and ended his season early in 2025.

"I've just got to move forward," Bako-Bewele told reporters at his locker. "It's definitely not what I anticipated happening. You've just got to get back to work and start thinking about next year."

Bako-Bewele, 27, is playing on a four-year, $88 million contract extension that runs through the 2029 season. When healthy, he's arguably Green Bay's best offensive lineman.

Bako-Bewele sustained the injury in the first quarter of Sunday's game. The Packers didn't know the extent of the injury at the time, but head coach Matt LaFleur told reporters postgame that Bako-Bewele could be out "for a long time."

Second-year pro Anthony Belton projects to move into Bako-Bewele's spot at right tackle. A second-round pick in the 2025 draft, Belton played in 14 games, including seven starts, as a rookie last season.

With Bako-Bewele recovering from his previous patellar tendon injury, Belton got reps as Green Bay's starting right tackle during the offseason. He'll now have the opportunity to establish himself as a starting-caliber NFL tackle. The Packers are certainly hoping that's the case.

Are Packers still a realistic Super Bowl contender?

A Packers team that started the season with Super Bowl aspirations looks little like a contender through two weeks. Green Bay gave up 22 unanswered fourth-quarter points in a Week 1 loss to the rival Minnesota Vikings , then narrowly avoided an 0-2 start with a rally from a 10-point fourth-quarter deficit for a 20-17 overtime win over the Jets on Sunday.

With starting running back Josh Jacobs on the commissioner's exempt list , the Packers rank last in the NFL in rushing with 64.5 yards per game. Now they've lost arguably their best offensive lineman. Reed's playing status, meanwhile, has taken a back seat to concern for his general health.

The shorthanded Packers face a short Week 3 with a Thursday night game against the Atlanta Falcons . From there, they'll face the Buccaneers, Bears, Cowboys, Lions, Panthers , Patriots and Vikings before a Week 11 bye.

The good news on the horizon for Green Bay is that All-Pro pass rusher Micah Parsons remains optimistic about his return from last season's ACL tear amid reports that a Week 6 return vs. his former Cowboys is a possibility.

articles.title: Gisele Bündchen reportedly slammed Bill Belichick for refusing to treat Tom Brady like a man
articles.summary: NFL News: Tom Brady spent two decades building a legacy in New England, but six Super Bowl titles could not shield him from the strain of playing under Bill Bel.
articles.body: Tom Brady spent two decades building a legacy in New England, but six Super Bowl titles could not shield him from the strain of playing under Bill Belichick. Behind the Patriots' success, their partnership faced growing personal tensions. Now, author Lars Anderson has brought fresh attention to a private confrontation involving Gisele Bündchen and team owner Robert Kraft. The meeting offers a glimpse into the frustration surrounding Brady's final years with the Patriots, when the quarterback's achievements appeared to do little to soften Belichick's demanding approach.Gisele Bündchen challenged Robert Kraft over Bill Belichick's treatment of Tom BradyIn his upcoming book, Brady: An American Story and the Price of Greatness, Anderson recounts a meeting at Kraft's home involving Brady and Bündchen. According to the author, the supermodel voiced her frustration over how Belichick treated her husband, despite his central role in the Patriots' historic run.“Gisele and Tom went over to Bob Kraft’s house late in his career with the Patriots,” Anderson said in an exclusive interview on Monday. “Gisele essentially told Kraft, I think she said, ‘Bill doesn’t treat Tommy like an effing man.’”The remark highlights the personal cost of Brady's relentless pursuit of success. Anderson's book, set for release on September 29, draws on more than 350 interviews. Brady did not cooperate with the project.Belichick's blunt coaching style reportedly played a major role in the growing divide. Even after Brady became the face of the Patriots dynasty, the coach continued to challenge him in front of teammates.“One famous anecdote is when he said, ‘Johnny Foxborough could have made that f****** throw,’” Anderson said. “And Tom took it.”Anderson describes the repeated criticism as a “slow-acting poison” that gradually damaged the relationship between the two NFL legends.Tom Brady and Bill Belichick's Patriots relationship reached a breaking pointAnderson's account echoes a scene from Jeff Benedict's The Dynasty, which detailed a similar confrontation after New England's Super Bowl LII loss to Philadelphia.“I heard Gisele say, ‘That effin’ Belichick, he doesn’t treat my Tommy like a man,’” Kraft recalled, according to Benedict's book.Kraft reportedly offered to help Brady leave New England if that was what he wanted. Tensions also grew over Belichick's restrictions on Brady's longtime trainer, Alex Guerrero, who lost access to the Patriots' sideline and team charter.Brady stayed for the 2019 season and won another Super Bowl before leaving for Tampa Bay in 2020. He then captured a seventh championship with the Buccaneers, adding another remarkable chapter to his career.Brady had also openly acknowledged the challenge of playing under Belichick in 2018.“He has a management style \[with\] players, and he would say, ‘Look, I’m not the easiest coach to play for,’” Brady said at the time. “I agree. articles.title: Bengals erase unwanted NFL-long 65-game streak vs. Texans
articles.summary: The Bengals kept Houston out of the end zone and ended the NFL's longest active run of games allowing a touchdown.
articles.body:
The Cincinnati Bengals ' redone defense finally wiped out an unwanted streak in Sunday's 20-6 win over the Houston Texans .

The Associated Press noted that Cincinnati held an opponent without a touchdown for the first time since Week 3 of the 2022 season against the New York Jets . The Bengals had allowed at least one touchdown in 65 consecutive games, the NFL's longest active streak.

The Buffalo Bills now own the league's longest such run at 47 games and counting.

Cincinnati forced Houston to settle for two field goals despite the Texans reaching the red zone four times. The Bengals also generated four sacks and 27 pressures across 62 dropbacks while blitzing on 13.3% of those plays, the lowest rate by any defense Sunday.

That production supported defensive coordinator Al Golden's belief that his unit is establishing a clear identity. Five Bengals registered at least four pressures, and Boye Mafe 's seven tied his career high.

The Bengals' postgame notes showed Houston managed only 60 rushing yards and converted five of 17 third downs. Cincinnati also stopped all four fourth-down attempts, including Dexter Lawrence 's tackle for loss at the Bengals' 18-yard line.

The Bengals are 2-0 and head to Pittsburgh in Week 3 with a defense that has supplied more than early-season optimism.

articles.title: 2-0 vs. 0-2: The undefeated NFL teams you should doubt — and the winless ones you should still believe in
articles.summary: The good times aren't expected to last for the Raiders, but it doesn't mean we can't enjoy them. And, c'mon, Houston. Are we really doing a repeat of last se...
articles.body:
Week 2 delivered quite the whiplash for many clubs. Probably none typified both ends of the spectrum more than the Chicago Bears , who went from 59-point juggernauts in the season opener to an outfit that couldn't cross the end zone due to … rain?

As for the teams that stayed consistent winners or losers after two games, this week we had Yahoo Sports writers Frank Schwab, Jay Busbee, Jori Epstein and Eric Edholm look at the clubs that shouldn't panic and ones that could be fooling us all.

Schwab: The Raiders are improved, but beating the Dolphins in 2026 doesn't move the needle and the Chargers are absolutely shellshocked . Give credit to the Raiders, who should be better when Brock Bowers returns. First-year head coach Klint Kubiak is changing the perception of Las Vegas overnight. It's not out of the question the Raiders could be in playoff contention all season. But if we're picking a team for this exercise, this has to be the pick.

Busbee: Obvious answer is the Raiders, but all congratulations to them for winning the games in front of them.

Let's look at Cincinnati , which is one Joe Burrow hangnail away from dropping five straight yet is at one-third of its entire 2025 season's win total. The Bengals ' short-term schedule looks incredibly favorable — Steelers twice, Dolphins, Falcons and Titans all await in the next few weeks — so if they have even a hint of a struggle through that run, it'll speak volumes about this team's viability. Let's check back with Cincinnati in mid-November and see what's up.

Epstein: The Las Vegas Raiders are my true answer, but I'll mix it up for the sake of reader interest and as a nod to Frank, whose machine-like work ethic led him to once again file his answers first. Instead, I'll take the San Francisco 49ers .

I actually fully believe a healthy 49ers team could win the Super Bowl. I think an 80% healthy 49ers team could make a run for it, too. But the Niners have taken a series of bets on players who are aging, boast an injury history or both. NFL wisdom says past injury history is the best predictor of future injury. If the health bug (that of course has nothing to do with the substation) strikes more than wide receiver De'Zhaun Stribling, the promising rookie already expected to miss 10 weeks due to surgery, can the 49ers make the cut in the league's toughest division?

Edholm: The Raiders have beaten two 0-2 teams, including a Dolphins team that's the only one not to have the lead in a game yet this season. Bully for them!

Look, Kirk Cousins has been solid with an underwhelming receiving corps, and the defensive pressure has been impressive so far. It looks like keeping Maxx Crosby has been a good thing to this point. But the next five games, all against competitive teams, will tell us whether these Raiders are for real or not. Don't forget the Arizona Cardinals started 2-0 last year and finished with three wins.

Schwab: I still want to believe in the Texans , even though going 0-2 at home to start the season is brutal. Don't forget, they were 0-3 last season and finished 12-5.

I still believe Houston 's defense will be one of the best in the NFL by the end of the season. Its offense needs Nico Collins . We saw that in Week 2. If Collins' injury isn't too serious, there have been positive signs from the offense through two weeks. DeMeco Ryans is a good head coach and he'll figure things out. The Texans will need to steal some road wins to make up for a poor start.

Busbee: I very much want to believe in the Chargers , because I love the idea, in theory, of Mike McDaniel unlocking Justin Herbert . In practice, it's proving much tougher to teach that sort-of-old-dog some new pocket tricks, and the Chargers have the most murderous short-term schedule you could design without throwing in the '85 Bears and the Brady-Moss Patriots .

If they can survive the next five weeks and then start picking off division wins, they can drift-slide their way into the playoffs. And if I keep asking, maybe Santa will one day bring me a new PlayStation. I still believe that could happen, too.

Epstein: " Believe" might be a strong word to describe my decision to vote for the Indianapolis Colts here, especially as receiver Alec Pierce is expected to miss weeks after aggravating his surgically repaired heel. But I defined "belief" as belief in the possibility of making the playoffs, and I think the Colts' chance is better than any of their 0-2 counterparts.

The AFC South standings are their first benefit: No division team is 2-0; the Tennessee Titans and Houston Texans join the Colts at 0-2.

The Colts' schedule gives me a second reason for optimism: While hosting the Texans this weekend might be tricky, the Colts then face a Commanders team likely without quarterback Jayden Daniels , a Steelers team that hasn't figured out its offense and a Titans team whose early-season grit almost gave them my nod here over the Colts but nonetheless doesn't have the talent Indianapolis has.

As Daniel Jones settles into his post-Achilles tear year, the Colts can and should lean on Jonathan Taylor to control the clock. Taking the Chiefs to overtime is reason for optimism. So I believe … that the Colts are the most likely 0-2 team to make the playoffs right now. Time will tell how likely that actually makes them.

Edholm: I am not quitting the Texans. They dropped two games against good teams. They were 0-2 (and then 0-3) a year ago and would have been dangerous with a little more offense.

I know the C.J. Stroud vibes aren't great right now, and the offensive line ones are worse. I also hate that the two losses were in Houston, where the Texans play only twice more until mid-November. But if there's an 0-2 club to get behind, it's the one with the great defense in the division that has one victory combined right now.

articles.title: Brock Bowers Injury Update, Return Timeline Revealed in Latest NFL Rumors After Raiders Start 2-0
articles.summary: The Las Vegas Raiders are off to a somewhat surprising 2-0 start, and they could get one of their star players back this week.
articles.body:
The Las Vegas Raiders are off to a somewhat surprising 2-0 start, and they could get one of their star players back this week.

NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported Tuesday that tight end Brock Bowers is expected to be back with the Raiders this week against the New Orleans Saints after missing the start of the season with a knee injury.

Bowers missed the Raiders' season opener against the Miami Dolphins and had a meniscus trim procedure earlier this month after injuring his knee during training camp.

There was initially hope that he'd be able to return for Week 2, but he ended up missing the game against the Los Angeles Chargers. The Raiders still managed to take care of business, beating their divisional rival 26-14.

Bowers had a standout rookie season that saw him collect 1,194 yards and five touchdowns. Injuries struck in Year 2, and Bowers ended up missing five games because of knee troubles. He still finished the 2025 campaign with 680 yards and seven scores.

With Bowers out, Michael Mayer has assumed the starting tight end role for the Raiders, recording nine receptions for 55 yards through two games. Las Vegas inked Mayer to a three-year, $45 million extension before the season, clearly showing that it values him alongside Bowers.

Wide receiver Tre Tucker has been the focal point of the passing attack to start the season, and he's picked up seven receptions and 146 yards through two games. Running back Ashton Jeanty has also done well to aid the offense, rushing for 150 yards so far.

But while the Raiders have gotten strong play from a few skill players, potentially having Bowers back on Sunday would give them even more of an edge.

Las Vegas appeared to be in for another rebuilding year coming into the season, but a 2-0 start perhaps says otherwise. If the Raiders can keep Bowers and other key players healthy, they could make a surprising run.

articles.title: Patriots Quietly Sign 4-Year NFL Veteran After Eli Raridon Injury
articles.summary: The Patriots quietly signed a four-year NFL veteran after Eli Raridon suffered an injury, adding depth before their next game. The post Patriots Quietly Sign...
articles.body:
The New England Patriot s added a four-year NFL veteran to their thin tight end room Tuesday, signing former Miami Dolphin Tanner Conner to the practice squad, in a move first reported by Mike Reiss of ESPN.com.

The move gives coach Mike Vrabel a proven body to call on if rookie Eli Raridon's thigh injury lingers into next week's trip to Jacksonville .

New England made the addition the same day it placed guard Mike Onwenu on injured reserve and signed punter Mitch Wishnowsky to the 53-man roster.

Conner arrived on the heels of a Monday workout that Reiss first reported. The Patriots brought in four free-agent tight ends for tryouts, and Conner's name rose to the top of the list.

Devin Culp of Washington, Lance Mason of Wisconsin and Australian tight end Patrick Murtagh also took reps that day , though Conner's NFL mileage separated him from that group.

Tanner Conner's Path to the New England Patriots

Conner, 28, grew up in Kent, Washington, and starred at Kentridge High School as a defensive back, receiver and hurdler. He won a state championship in the 300-meter hurdles and was recruited more heavily for track than football.

At Idaho State, he converted that speed into a five-year receiving career, catching 136 passes for 2,384 yards and 15 touchdowns from 2016 through 2021. His best season came during 2021, when he hauled in 34 catches for 685 yards and earned first-team all-conference honors.

Conner also thrived on the track, winning the Big Sky indoor title in the 60-meter hurdles and setting a conference record of 7.73 seconds, according to the Idaho State Journal .

He also picked up a criminology degree with a psychology minor at Idaho State, then a graduate degree in athletic administration.

His father Andy Conner played linebacker at Oregon and spent time on Seattle and St. Louis preseason rosters.

Miami signed Conner as an undrafted free agent in 2022 and converted him to tight end. He spent four seasons with the Dolphins before finishing 2025 on the Giants ' practice squad. New York released him Aug. 30. His NFL resume now includes 12 catches for 107 yards over 33 games.

New England Patriots' Tight End Depth Chart Takes a Hit

Hunter Henry remains the unquestioned starter and a team captain. Raridon, a third-round pick out of Notre Dame, had posted the biggest catch of his rookie season, a 30-yard grab, before he limped out of Sunday's 20-3 win over Pittsburgh .

New England had already moved on from tight end Shane Zylstra , releasing him from the practice squad Sept. 15 to bring back safety Elliott Davison, according to the team's updated tight end depth chart.

That left Henry and waiver claim Cameron Latu as the only healthy tight ends on the field. Undrafted rookie Tanner Arkin, a blocking specialist, sat out that game as a healthy scratch, and free-agent addition Julian Hill has been on injured reserve since June with a knee injury.

The Patriots aren't expecting Conner to push for targets. His NFL history points to a depth and special-teams role, the kind of assignment where his converted-receiver athleticism and tryout-day experience matter more than raw production. If Raridon can't go in Jacksonville, New England now has a tested option ready to be elevated on short notice.

articles.title: 49ers bring In two-time Super Bowl WR as injuries begin to pile up
articles.summary: The San Francisco 49ers are turning to veteran wide receiver Brandin Cooks for help as injuries continue to pile up, adding the former first-round pick and n...
articles.body:
The San Francisco 49ers are adding an experienced weapon to their receiving corps as injuries continue to test their depth early in the season.

Veteran wide receiver Brandin Cooks is signing with San Francisco 's practice squad, according to ESPN's Adam Schefter. The initial plan is to give the 32-year-old time to learn the offense and get prepared before potentially contributing on game days.

Cooks arrives at an important time for San Francisco. The 49ers have already dealt with injuries to receivers Ricky Pearsall , De'Zhaun Stribling and Demarcus Robinson . Veteran Mike Evans is also dealing with a hip injury that could require the team to monitor his workload this week.

Adding Cooks gives San Francisco another proven option with more than a decade of NFL experience.

The New Orleans Saints originally selected Cooks with the No. 20 overall pick in the 2014 NFL Draft after his college career at Oregon State. He spent his first three seasons in New Orleans before beginning a journey that has taken him across the league.

He returned to New Orleans in 2025, but that reunion ended in November when the Saints waived him following his request to be released. Cooks later signed with Buffalo and finished the season with the Bills.

His Buffalo tenure included a memorable and controversial moment in the playoffs. During overtime of the Bills' divisional-round loss to Denver , Cooks appeared to secure a deep pass from Josh Allen before Broncos cornerback Ja'Quan McMillian took possession as Cooks went to the ground. Officials ruled the play an interception, and Buffalo never regained possession.

Cooks brings extensive postseason experience to San Francisco as well. He appeared in consecutive Super Bowls with New England and Los Angeles , although both teams lost.

Over 12 NFL seasons, Cooks has accumulated 734 receptions for 9,811 receiving yards and 62 total touchdowns.

Now, he will attempt to provide valuable veteran depth for a 49ers offense navigating several injuries at wide receiver.

articles.title: How Tom Brady went from being the 199th overall pick in the 2000 NFL Draft to building a staggering $650 million net worth
articles.summary: NFL News: Tom Brady was not supposed to be this. Not even close. The 2000 NFL Draft came and went, 198 players heard their names before his, and the New England.
articles.body: Tom Brady was not supposed to be this. Not even close. The 2000 NFL Draft came and went, 198 players heard their names before his, and the New England Patriots finally took a chance on a skinny Michigan quarterback in the sixth round. Twenty-six years later, that same quarterback is worth $650 million and owns a piece of an NFL franchise. What happened in between is one of the most unlikely financial stories in American sports history.How did Tom Brady become so wealthy after retiring from the NFL?The $333 million Brady earned over 23 NFL seasons sounds enormous until you consider how much he left on the table. For most of his prime years in New England, he was deliberately underpaid relative to market value, restructuring contracts to give the team more salary-cap room. He won championships instead of chasing pay raises, and for a long time, that was the trade-off.What changed everything was what came after football. In May 2022, while Brady was technically still a quarterback, Fox Sports signed him to a 10-year, $375 million broadcast deal to become the network's lead NFL analyst. That is $37.5 million per year, which works out to more than what any team ever paid him in a single season. He finally made his debut in September 2024 alongside Kevin Burkhardt, called Super Bowl LIX in his first season in the booth, and returned for a second season in 2025. If paid evenly across the contract, his first two seasons alone represent around $75 million in broadcast income.So yes, retirement has paid Brady considerably better than most of his playing years did.How much is Tom Brady's Las Vegas Raiders ownership stake worth now?Tom Brady's most valuable asset right now is not a Fox paycheck. It is a 5% ownership stake in the Las Vegas Raiders that he purchased alongside Knighthead Capital co-founder Tom Wagner in October 2024, following a long and complicated approval process by NFL owners.Together, Brady and Wagner bought a combined 10% stake for $220 million, with Brady personally spending around $110 million for his half, plus a share of roughly $24 million in additional league-related fees tied to the franchise's relocation history. The purchase price implied a team valuation somewhere around $3.5 billion at the time, which was well below what independent estimates suggested the Raiders were actually worth.Then in May 2026, a separate group of investors acquired more than 25% of the Raiders in a transaction that pegged the franchise's value at approximately $9.9 billion. Using that benchmark, Brady's 5% stake now carries a headline valuation of close to $500 million. He paid roughly $110 million for something that appears to be worth about four and a half times that today. There are restrictions on how quickly he can sell and the NFL limits what minority owners can do, but the unrealized appreciation is real and it is extraordinary.He has also moved beyond passive investment. Brady now advises the Raiders' front office on football decisions, and heading into the 2026 season, he is reportedly helping develop Fernando Mendoza, the rookie quarterback Las Vegas took with the first overall pick in the 2026 draft.What other business ventures and endorsements have added to Tom Brady's net worth?Beyond the Raiders and Fox, Tom Brady has spent years building a portfolio of brands and businesses that trade on his identity as someone who refused to age normally.His TB12 Method, built around pliability training, nutrition, and recovery, became both a brand and a business. He launched BRADY Brand, a men's apparel line, and later combined both ventures with athletic company NOBULL, giving him an equity stake in the merged business. He co-founded Autograph during the NFT boom and started 199 Productions, a film and television company whose name is a nod to his draft position.Endorsement income during his playing years was substantial, estimated at $10 to $20 million annually at various points, with brand relationships spanning Under Armour, UGG, Tag Heuer, Aston Martin, Subway, and others. His career endorsement total is well north of $100 million.Not everything worked. Brady and his then-wife Gisele Bundchen became brand ambassadors for FTX in 2021, taking equity stakes in the cryptocurrency exchange. When FTX collapsed into bankruptcy in November 2022, Brady's shares were wiped out entirely. The potential loss has been estimated at tens of millions of dollars in paper value, gone overnight.Brady also owns a minority stake in the WNBA's Las Vegas Aces and has invested in English soccer club Birmingham City, so his portfolio continues to grow outside American football.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Let Caleb Williams Cry. His Authenticity And Sensitivity Make Him A Superstar.
articles.summary: Caleb Williams has brought in a new set of emotions into the NFL, and you shouldn't have a problem with it.
articles.body: Caleb Williams has a habit of making us — the NFL world — uncomfortable. He doesn’t care about optics. He doesn’t waste thought on what the average NFL fan (or GM or coach) might think. He reacts authentically. He’s sensitive. He feels. He hurts — publicly. You don’t see that often in the NFL. You don’t see that enough, frankly. Think back to when he sought out his mother to cry in her arms at USC. Think back to when he used to let his mother paint his nails. Think back to that photoshoot where Williams was sitting in a — how to put this? — vulnerable position. And, of course, think back to Sunday when he sat on the injury cart and pumped his fist with tears in his eyes. That’s the incident that’s all over social media. You can guess by now: I don’t have a problem with it. And it’s hilarious to watch people crying on social media with criticisms about … another man crying. But it’s no surprise. Hypocrisy isn’t hard to find on X, Instagram or TikTok. The criticism is getting absurd. The memes — well, some of them are objectively funny. The silliness is fair, now that we know he could play again in Week 3. This is 2026. Williams isn’t just a public figure — he’s the NFL’s rising superstar, fed to fans all offseason through the media and Madden hype. He has opted into some of that, but not all. (The Bears and Williams, for example, declined a one-on-one interview when I visited camp this summer, in part because the buzz was going too far.) After putting up 59 points in Week 1, the Bears' matchup against the Vikings was the most anticipated matchup of Week 2. When he does something objectively theatrical, people will respond with good-natured jokes. But the genuine pearl-clutching and hand-wringing? The idea that the injury cart is somehow sacred and reserved only for career-ending injuries? Get out of here. Let’s go back to the play where the injury happened for context. Trying to escape a sack late in the fourth quarter, Williams slid. He held his hamstring and screamed, captured clearly by the broadcast. He banged the turf with his fist in frustration. The team got out the cart, and — this part you’ve surely seen — he covered his face with a towel, eventually pulling it away to show his red, watery eyes. He pumped the air, like he was Kobe Bryant after tearing his Achilles. This is high drama worthy of reality television. But folks, I hate to break it to you. The NFL is reality television. The NFL is all about its drama. It’s no mystery why Madden wanted to put Williams on its cover. He’s fascinating on and off the field. He’s a great football player. But he’s also unique. And it’s this sensitivity that — I think — makes him different than the average NFL player, coach or fan. I can see why Williams was upset. It’s not all that different than the last time we saw him publicly crying after that big loss at USC. It was the sheer disappointment of a missed opportunity. He was on the 6-yard line — just a handful of yards away from a go-ahead touchdown. In an ugly game. Against a division rival. If he and the Bears had scored, no one would have cared that the Vikings won the X’s and O’s and stymied what was supposed to be a historic Bears offense. That’s a tough thing for an injury to take away. We also have no idea what that injury might have felt like — the level of pain. But I’m sure everyone can relate to a disappointment of this magnitude. The season looked so promising, even in that ugly game. For the rest of the fourth quarter, it looked like Williams’ season might be in jeopardy. Williams had to reconcile with his game — and his season — ending in major disappointment. Then we got the first sign of good news. "I'm actually happy it's nothing with the knee. That was my first inclination," coach Ben Johnson said during a postgame press conference. "But yeah, the hamstring could be pretty damaging as well. So, we'll see how bad it is tomorrow and we'll go from there. … We need the points desperately at that point. It's a shame." Now here’s a criticism that I’ll buy: Williams’ theatrics distracted the team’s focus at the game’s most crucial moments. "Everybody wants to keep morale up," Bears defensive lineman Grady Jarrett told reporters after the game. "Because Caleb is the guy here, and so nobody wants to see him go down. Definitely have got to rally up, do more. We’ve got to finish the game at the end of the day." It’s a bit hypothetical for my taste to wonder if the Bears would've won if Williams hadn’t taken the cart, hadn’t pumped his fist and didn't have tears in his eyes? If the answer is yes, then the Bears have to examine their team-wide focus before examining Williams’, because one man’s tears should not leave the other 47 players without resolve. Football is a sport where toughness is — quite literally — on a player’s scouting report. Obviously, this series of events left us questioning Williams’ toughness. But bigger than that, if Williams is a superstar and he isn’t "tough," can he be successful in the NFL? The way I see it: The tears don’t matter. The hamstring injury does. If there was a way for Williams to play through the injury, then there’s a problem there, because his departure worsened their chances. If there was no way for Williams to get back on the field, then what are we arguing about? The manner that he left the field? Again, get out of here. Let’s all take this opportunity to take a deep breath and try to get comfortable with seeing a grown man cry. From my vantage, that’s what this is about. People don’t like seeing their quarterback cry. I’m not one of them. I’m all for it. FOX SPORTS NEWSLETTERYour teams. Your sports. articles.title: “Every child deserves to be confident”: Patrick Mahomes’ $15,000 literacy move helped put nearly 6,000 books in Kansas City kids’ hands while giving homeless children a fresh start
articles.summary: NFL News: Patrick Mahomes has found another way to help Kansas City children, and this one starts with a book. On May 31, 2025, his 15 and the Mahomies Foundati.
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes has found another way to help Kansas City children, and this one starts with a book. On May 31, 2025, his 15 and the Mahomies Foundation announced a $15,000 donation to the Kansas City Public Library’s Summer Reading Program. The money helped the library purchase nearly 6,000 books for local children and support its effort to reduce summer learning loss.The donation added another piece to Mahomes’ literacy work. His foundation had already backed reading programmes across Kansas City, while his #ReadFor15 campaign encourages children to spend at least 15 minutes reading each day. Patrick Mahomes turned $15,000 into nearly 6,000 books for Kansas City kidsThe Kansas City Public Library received the $15,000 award as part of its continuing partnership with the 15 and the Mahomies Foundation. The money funded nearly 6,000 books that the library planned to distribute to Kansas City children through its 2025 Summer Reading Program.The foundation also pointed to summer learning loss. It cited studies showing that students in third through fifth grade can lose as much as 20% of their previous reading gains during the summer break.The library had a strong base to build on. Its 2024 Summer Reading Program attracted a record 15,060 registered participants. In 2025, the programme ran from May 30 through August 15. Every person who registered received a free book, while participants could also complete a five-book challenge and earn a reward.Mahomes spoke about the value of reading in the foundation’s May 31 announcement.“Reading every day is so important. It helps us grow, learn, and dream big,” Patrick Mahomes said in the announcement of his foundation’s partnership with the Kansas City Public Library.The donation also followed Mahomes’ March 31 appearance at the Read for 15 Reading Rally at T-Mobile Center. articles.body:
Chicago Bears quarterback Caleb Williams screamed in pain after a non-contact hamstring injury in Week 2, raising fears of a more serious injury. Fans and analysts have discussed Williams' reaction to the injury.

Many were sympathetic to his on-field show of emotion, while others accused him of being over-dramatic. The debate has also reignited a social media feud between Emmanuel Acho and Leonard Fournette .

Emmanuel Acho, Leonard Fournette Reignite Beef Amid Caleb Williams Injury

Acho and Fournette have gone back and forth before. But this time their back-and-forth started when Fournette reacted to Acho's comments on Williams' injury . Apparently, Acho was not too pleased with Fournette's reaction.

"Here's my thing, Leonard. I am too old to fight anybody. But you know what's interesting? People who rush to fight only train their body and haven't trained their brain."

"Because I've trained my brain, why would I only resort to using my body? Leonard, I really question your intelligence because you can't even pronounce a four-letter word. Acho, not Echo," Acho began .

"The biggest word you probably even know is your name. But that's probably why they call you 'Lenny' because you probably couldn't even spell your own name… I'm not going to try and address you physically because you got that…"

"You're retired, so hang up the athletic dreams. Pick up a book. You don't need to be hooked on creatine, you don't need to be hooked on the weights, maybe try hooked on Phonics," Acho continued.

Acho and Fournette both played in the NFL. The Cleveland Browns selected Acho, a linebacker, in the sixth round of the 2012 NFL Draft. He spent time with Cleveland, Philadelphia , and the New York Giants , but played regular-season games only for Philadelphia.

Fournette, by contrast, was a running back. The Jacksonville Jaguars selected him fourth overall in the 2017 NFL Draft. He topped 1,000 rushing yards twice, both times with Jacksonville. Fournette also played for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and the Buffalo Bills .

Both men had different levels of success in their careers. Acho last appeared in a regular-season game in 2014, while the Philadelphia Eagles won Super Bowl 52 after the 2017 season. Fournette, on the other hand, won Super Bowl 55 with the Buccaneers.

Meanwhile, Chicago confirmed that Williams suffered a hamstring injury. The team currently considers him week-to-week.

"I gotta still talk with our trainer here; we'll do that here shortly, and I'll have the lowdown from him, but it sounds like it's week-to-week and he will likely miss some time," head coach Ben Johnson said of the injury , via NFL.com.

The Bears will next face the Eagles on Monday Night Football in Week 3.

articles.title: ‘Take That, Dan Orlovsky!’ — NFL Legend Terrell Owens Goes After ESPN Analyst, Settles Jalen Hurts vs. Justin Herbert Debate Once and For All
articles.summary: The greatness of a quarterback has never been an objective measure. But over the offseason, two stylistically polar-opposite players, Jalen Hurts and Justin...
articles.body:
The greatness of a quarterback has never been an objective measure. But over the offseason, two stylistically polar-opposite players, Jalen Hurts and Justin Herbert , have been at two ends of the spectrum for discourse around the position.

While some prefer the intangibles and undeniable success that comes with the Philadelphia Eagles star, others prefer the raw talent and arm strength of the Los Angeles Chargers QB1. But two weeks into the 2026 season, Terrell Owens is ready to settle the debate once and for all.

Terrell Owens Chooses Between Jalen Hurts and Justin Herbert

Over the offseason, analysts staked their claim on the two quarterbacks. Despite their wildly different resumes, Hurts, with two trips to the Super Bowl, landed at 56 on the NFL's Top 100 players list of 2026, while Herbert was far ahead at 39.

Unfortunately, some were sticking with their priors even after a disastrous Week 1 for the Chargers. After they lost to the woeful Arizona Cardinals 26-14, former quarterback turned analyst Dan Orlovsky claimed that Herbert was what a "quarterback should look like."

Now, after a second-straight disastrous week, as they lost to the Las Vegas Raiders 26-14, while Hurts led the Eagles to a 2-0 start, Owens is ready to run a victory lap on the former Detroit Lions quarterback.

"I saw the discussion with Dan Orlovsky. First of all, the idea that Dan Orlovsky, I think he's changed his tune a bit," the Hall of Fame wide receiver claimed on the "Get To The Point" podcast. "If you see what Jalen Hurts has done over the last four or five years, just imagine, just see what he did this past weekend."

BE THE GM OF YOUR FAVORITE TEAM: PFN's Free NFL Mock Draft Simulator

Going into detail about his accomplishments, he boiled it down to their Week 2 game against the Tennessee Titans . Despite an underwhelming game, Hurts was able to lead a game-winning drive in the waning moments of the game to give the Eagles the 24-20 win.

"I think it was maybe a minute or two left in the game. That's not a lot of time. And when you talk about clutch quarterbacks, Super Bowl-caliber quarterbacks, quarterbacks to lead you to victories, when you talk about leadership, this is what this guy possesses."

PREDICT THE NFL SEASON: PFN's Free NFL Playoff Predictor

After two weeks, even the raw numbers favor Hurts over Herbert. In PFN's Quarterback Impact Rankings , Hurts ranks at #11, while Herbert has fallen to the third-worst mark in the league.

"When you talk about a guy that can make all the plays with his feet, with his arm, that's what this guy, that's what he possesses in Jalen Hurts. This is what he's supposed to do. This is what you expect when you're a Philly fan. They expect these things. They don't want it to be this close. But I think he delivered. Take that, Dan Orlovsky. Take that."

It remains to be seen if this is the year that finally changes the perception of both Hurts and Herbert across media circles. But through two weeks, there hasn't been much doubt about who has been better among the two.

articles.title: Patriots news: Adam Vinatieri makes Guinness World FG record 5 years after retiring
articles.summary: Former New England Patriots kicker Adam Vinatieri built his legendary career on delivering in freezing, high-stakes moments. Years after stepping away from t...
articles.body:
Former New England Patriots kicker Adam Vinatieri built his legendary career on delivering in freezing, high-stakes moments. Years after stepping away from the gridiron, the NFL icon took that reputation to extreme heights, quite literally.

On Tuesday, the four-time Super Bowl champion officially claimed a Guinness World Record for the highest altitude field goal in history, sending a kick through the uprights at 3454 meters (11,332 feet) above sea level on the Jungfraujoch in the Swiss Alps. Standing on snow-covered ground against the scenic backdrop known as the "Top of Europe," Vinatieri proved his leg still has plenty of power.

"Snow is simply part of my time with the Patriots ," Vinatieri said . "But kicking a field goal at 3,454 meters is something completely different from anything I've ever seen in the NFL. You feel the altitude with every breath you take, your heart rate is different, your rhythm is different."

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

An official Guinness World Record adjudicator certified the achievement on site. The event was organized alongside the Patriots to build excitement for the franchise's upcoming international regular-season clash against the Detroit Lions in Munich, Germany.

For football fans, seeing Vinatieri master harsh winter conditions is nothing new. Over a storied 24-season career split between New England and the Indianapolis Colts , he established himself as the most clutch kicker in league history. Vinatieri retires as the NFL's all-time leading scorer with 2,673 points while converting 599 out of 715 career field goal attempts (83.8%) and holding the postseason scoring record with 238 points.

From his iconic 45-yard blizzard kick in the 2001 playoffs to multiple Super Bowl game-winners. Vinatieri has always shined in sub-zero weather. Now, even in retirement, the legendary placekicker continues to prove that distance and freezing temperatures are no match for his right leg.

articles.title: Nick Sirianni’s winning percentage places him among NFL legends
articles.summary: Nick Sirianni’s.701 winning percentage places him alongside four Hall of Fame coaches in an exclusive group of NFL winners
articles.body:
Nick Sirianni's success is becoming increasingly difficult to contextualize without mentioning some of the greatest coaches in NFL history.

Philadelphia's 2-0 start improved Sirianni's career record to 61-26, giving him a .701 winning percentage. According to Reuben Frank of NBC Sports Philadelphia , via Eagles Communications , he is one of five coaches in league history to coach at least 50 games and win 70% of them.

Guy Chamberlin finished with a .784 winning percentage, followed by John Madden at .759, Vince Lombardi at .738, and George Allen at .712. Sirianni is the only member of that group to coach a game since 1980. He is also approaching another significant place in Eagles history. Sirianni needs three victories to pass Greasy Neale's total of 63 and move into second place on the franchise's coaching wins list. Andy Reid holds the record with 130.

Sirianni added another distinction with Philadelphia's victory over Tennessee. He became the fourth coach to win each of his first six road openers. Allen won seven consecutive road openers from 1966 through 1972. Mike McCarthy won six from 2006 through 2011, while Sean McVay won seven from 2017 through 2023.

Sirianni's tenure has included criticism, coordinator changes, and disappointing postseason exits. It has also produced consistent winning, multiple division titles and two Super Bowl appearances. The Eagles have areas to correct after two uneven victories. Their head coach's record shows they have consistently found solutions during his tenure.

articles.title: Week 3 Start 'Em, Sit 'Em Review for Fantasy Football's Top Fringe Starters
articles.summary: As we prepare for another week of NFL action, it's safe to say that the 2026 season has been filled with surprises. We've seen sleepers emerge as stars, standouts disappoint, and several top fantasy performers suffer significant injuries.
articles.body:
As we prepare for another week of NFL action, it's safe to say that the 2026 season has been filled with surprises. We've seen sleepers emerge as stars, standouts disappoint, and several top fantasy performers suffer significant injuries.

This has likely left many managers relying on fringe starters before bye weeks have even gotten underway. Fortunately, the matchups should allow some second-tier stars to shine in Week 3.

Here, you'll find some start/sit recommendations based on past performances, projected roles, and individual matchups. All picks and analysis are based on point-per-reception (PPR) scoring.

Start: David Montgomery, RB, Houston Texans

Houston Texans running back David Montgomery had a strong debut against the Buffalo Bills but struggled to find running room against the Cincinnati Bengals in Week 2. The absence of star wide receiver Nico Collins likely had a lot to do with that.

Montgomery did catch a pair of passes with Collins out, but he finished with just 24 scrimmage yards and no touchdowns. Expect him to bounce back in Week 3, even though Collins appears unlikely to play again.

The Texans will visit the Indianapolis Colts, who have surrendered the third-most fantasy points to opposing running backs through two weeks. It's worth noting that the Colts have faced Derrick Henry and Kenneth Walker III in their first two games, but Indy's rebuilt linebacker group has left plenty to be desired.

Montgomery should be much more productive than he was this past week, and he should find the end zone in Indianapolis.

Sit: MarShawn Lloyd, RB, Green Bay Packers

MarShawn Lloyd has largely disappointed during his two-week audition to be the Green Bay Packers' starting running back. He did find the end zone against the New York Jets in Week 2, but he has tallied just 63 scrimmage yards and two catches while averaging 3.0 yards per carry through two weeks.

Managers who aren't ready to drop Lloyd should at least seek other options in Week 3. Green Bay has a short-week game and a less-than-ideal matchup against the Atlanta Falcons on Thursday night.

The Falcons haven't been good at much of anything through the first two weeks, though poor quarterback play has played a large role in their struggles. With Michael Penix Jr. getting the Week 3 start, Atlanta may actually score some points and prevent the Packers from grinding the game out on the ground.

And defending the run has been the Falcons' one strength through two weeks. Atlanta has surrendered the sixth-fewest fantasy points to opposing RBs.

Start: Deebo Samuel, WR, San Francisco 49ers

After spending a year away from the San Francisco 49ers, Deebo Samuel has stepped right back into a prominent role with the offense. He wasn't heavily used during Sunday's blowout win over the Miami Dolphins, though, finishing with three catches, one rush, and 35 scrimmage yards.

In Week 1 against the rival Los Angeles Rams, Samuel logged six catches, 60 yards, and a touchdown. He should have a similar performance in Week 3.

This week, the 49ers will face another NFC West foe in the Arizona Cardinals. While the Cardinals got blown out by the Seattle Seahawks on Sunday, they do have the offensive firepower to make things more competitive than the Dolphins did. If Trey McBride, Michael Wilson, and Jeremiyah Love can help Arizona keep pace early, the 49ers should turn to Samuel early and often.

And the Cardinals haven't been particularly good at slowing opposing receivers. They have surrendered the fifth-most fantasy points to the position.

Sit: Stefon Diggs, WR, Washington Commanders

Through two weeks, it would appear that Stefon Diggs has overtaken Terry McLaurin as the Washington Commanders' No. 1 receiver. He's logged at least four receptions and 45 yards in each contest, and he's caught three touchdown passes thus far.

Unfortunately, Diggs' production is probably poised to take a bit of a hit with Jayden Daniels on the sideline with a dislocated elbow. He did catch one of his two Week 2 touchdowns from backup Marcus Mariota, but with Mariota in the lineup, Diggs' ceiling is limited.

While Diggs should still be a solid matchup-based play, this week brings a matchup that should be avoided. Washington will host the Seahawks, which means Diggs likely faces a battle with Devon Witherspoon.

No team has surrendered fewer fantasy points to opposing receivers this season than Seattle.
