articles.title: Week 3 Waiver Wire Top Pickups and Drops Likely Available After Reviewing Box Scores
articles.summary: The NFL season has a way of reminding fantasy football enthusiasts that smart drafting is only part of the equation, and things have been no different in 2026.
articles.body:
The NFL season has a way of reminding fantasy football enthusiasts that smart drafting is only part of the equation, and things have been no different in 2026.

While we did see Week 1 disappointments like Ja'Marr Chase and Matthew Stafford bounce back in Week 2, we've also seen a rash of injuries that have taken top fantasy stars out of the equation for the short term. Since the season started, we've seen A.J. Brown, Zay Flowers, Caleb Williams, Jayden Daniels, Sam Darnold, Nico Collins, and Puka Nacua exit or miss time with injuries.

Even the smartest drafters can struggle to avoid the injury bug, but fortunately, they can find help on the waiver wire. Let's take a look at what we've seen over the first two weeks and identify some top pickups and drops for Week 3.

All picks and analysis are based on point-per-reception (PPR) scoring.

Let's start by saying that if New Orleans Saints quarterback Tyler Shough is available, he's a must-add. The second-year star has thrown for a league-high 662 yards with four passing touchdowns and a rushing score. He's only rostered in 49 percent of fantasy leagues.

Carolina Panthers quarterback Bryce Young is another terrific option. He's thrown for 648 yards and a league-high six touchdowns and has also run for a score. He's only rostered in 30 percent of leagues.

Young is also worth starting consideration this week against a Cleveland Browns defense that may be average at best. The Browns did get the best of Baker Mayfield in Week 2, but it's not a stretch to suggest that Mayfield beat himself more than he was beaten by his former team.

Cleveland was also atrocious in Week 1 and has surrendered the 11th-most fantasy points to opposing QBs through two weeks.

Add: Tank Bigsby, RB, Philadelphia Eagles

Star Philadelphia Eagles running back Saquon Barkley missed most of Week 2 with a stinger, though he did briefly return in the second half. He logged just four carries and finished with 20 scrimmage yards, and his health will bear watching heading into Week 3.

It's worth scooping up Eagles backup Tank Bigsby even if Barkley is in line to face the Chicago Bears. Chicago won't have quarterback Caleb Williams, and if the Philly gets up early, it may look to grind things out on the ground.

Chicago has surrendered the ninth-most fantasy points to opposing running backs this season.

Bigsby saw 15 touches in Week 2 and tallied 38 yards and a touchdown. He's rostered in 27 percent of fantasy leagues.

The Buffalo Bills saw new No. 1 receiver D.J. Moore go down with a shoulder injury against the Detroit Lions last Thursday. While the extra few days may allow Moore to return by Week 3, Buffalo isn't interested in rushing him back.

According to ESPN's Nick Suss , the Bills plan to "slow play" Moore's recovery.

This makes Khalil Shakir a tremendous waiver target, as he's likely to step into the No. 1 receiver role if Moore can't go. He's caught seven passes for 88 yards to this point in the season, but he'll have a much higher floor as Josh Allen's top perimeter target.

This week, Buffalo will host a Los Angeles Chargers team that has surrendered the eighth-most fantasy points to opposing receivers. Shakir is still only rostered in 60 percent of fantasy leagues.

Baker Mayfield has struggled with efficiency and turnovers through the first two weeks, and it's impossible to trust him moving forward. He hasn't found a true replacement for former go-to receiver Mike Evans, and the offense of new coordinator Zac Robinson remains a work in progress.

A Week 3 matchup with a terrific Minnesota Vikings defense makes a quick rebound unlikely for Mayfield. With quarterbacks like Shough and Young likely available, the Tampa Bay Buccaneers starter can be safely dumped.

Las Vegas Raiders tight end Michael Mayer can probably also be jettisoned this week. He was a serviceable fill-in while Brock Bowers was out, but Bowers appears likely to return to face the Saints in Week 3.

In his postgame press conference, Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak told reporters that Bowers was "very close" to playing on Sunday.

Jacksonville Jaguars running back Chris Rodriguez Jr . has clearly fallen behind Bhayshul Tuten in the Jags' committee backfield and hasn't seen enough of a receiver role to justify keeping in shallower leagues. However, he may be worth holding in deeper leagues due to the shortage of viable RB options this year.

Eagles rookie receiver Makai Lemon isn't worth keeping as he struggles to find a consistent role in the offense. Through two weeks, he's caught four of five targets for a mere nine yards.

*Fantasy scoring and roster information from FantasyPros .

articles.title: 2026 NFL Trade Block Big Board Entering Week 3
articles.summary: Any hope that Week 2 would bring clarity about who the top NFL contenders are dissipated rather quickly.
articles.body:
Any hope that Week 2 would bring clarity about who the top NFL contenders are dissipated rather quickly.

The San Francisco 49ers have been the only team that has looked truly dominant in each of its first two games, and some teams we expected to be bad entering the regular season have surprised. The Las Vegas Raiders, for example, are sitting at 2-0, and the New York Jets probably should be.

No team has surged or stumbled enough to solidify itself as a buyer or a seller ahead of the November 10 trade deadline. However, some squads are trending in one direction or another, and injuries continue to create needs that didn't exist ahead of Week 1.

Where might teams turn to fill those needs? Let's take a look.

Here's an updated look at our top 10 trade candidates, ranked by past production, upside, positional value, contract/cap implications, likely availability, and relevant recent rumors. You'll also find projected trade values based on factors such as position, player upside, player age, and any comparable deals, along with some logical suitors for each player.

10. Daron Payne, DT, Washington Commanders

Projected Trade Value: 2027 3rd-Round Pick

The Washington Commanders must quickly decide whether they can salvage their season after a 0-2 start and after losing quarterback Jayden Daniels to a dislocated elbow.

According to NFL Media's Ian Rapoport , Daniels will "consult with a variety of experts" before determining where he goes from here.

If the Commanders decide that it's not too soon to look ahead to 2027 and beyond, they should strongly consider moving defensive tackle Daron Payne. The 29-year-old is set to be a free agent in the spring, and while he's arguably Washington's most important impending free agent , there's no guarantee he'll want to return if the Commanders have another wasted campaign.

Payne would likely bring a Day 2 pick in return. He recorded 46 tackles and three sacks last season and has started both games in 2026.

Potential Suitors: Carolina Panthers, Green Bay Packers

Projected Trade Value: Conditional 2027 4th-Round Pick

Atlanta Falcons safety Jessie Bates III is another impending 2027 free agent who could become a prime trade chip if his team continues to struggle. The Falcons have looked like one of the worst teams in football over the first two weeks, though instability at quarterback has played a large role in that.

Michael Penix Jr. is set to make his 2026 debut on Thursday night, and if he can put one in the win column early, Bates will probably be off the table. He was arguably the team's most reliable defender last season, having started all 17 games and allowing an opposing passer rating of only 73.7 in coverage.

The 29-year-old has also made it known that he'd prefer to retire in Atlanta.

"My family loves it here. Why would I not want to be a Falcon?" Bates said, per Tori McElhaney of the team's official website.

If Penix cannot right the proverbial ship, though, Atlanta may start selling off veterans in preparation for the 2027 draft.

Potential Suitors: Detroit Lions, San Francisco 49ers

Projected Trade Value: 2027 1st-Round Pick, 2028 1st-Round Pick

Las Vegas Raiders edge-rusher Maxx Crosby isn't off our board just yet. However, the more the Raiders look like they could contend, the further down it he's going to slide.

The Raiders currently sit at 2-0, and they're probably not entertaining the prospect of trading their best defender right now. And while Crosby did ask for a trade early in the offseason—and Las Vegas tried to send him to the Baltimore Ravens—he reportedly shut down trade talk after the Ravens deal fell through.

According to Rapoport , the Los Angeles Rams were interested in Crosby before making the trade for Myles Garrett, but Crosby "let it be known to anyone interested that he did not want to be traded."

Still, the fact that the Raiders were previously open to moving one of the league's most disruptive defenders will keep him on other teams' radar between now and the November 10 trade deadline.

Expect the Raiders to get more than a few aggressive offers from Super Bowl hopefuls looking to boost their defensive fronts.

Potential Suitors: Dallas Cowboys, New England Patriots

Projected Trade Value: Conditional 7th-Round Draft Pick

The Tennessee Titans were far more competitive in Week 2 than they were in Week 1. However, they're still sitting at 0-2 and may soon have to recognize that they're probably not going to the playoffs in 2026.

If and when the Titans start looking ahead to next season, they should consider moving veterans who aren't part of the long-term picture. 30-year-old defensive lineman Solomon Thomas falls into this group.

Tennessee acquired Thomas in an offseason trade, a logical move at the time, as he had previously played for new head coach Robert Saleh. However, Thomas simply hasn't been a big piece of the defensive puzzle and has only played 28 percent of the defensive snaps through two games.

Thomas could, however, help another team in 2026. He logged 27 tackles and three tackles for loss in a rotational role with the Dallas Cowboys last season.

Potential Suitors: Atlanta Falcons, Baltimore Ravens

6. Khalil Mack, Edge, Los Angeles Chargers

The Los Angeles Chargers have been one of the NFL's biggest surprises through two weeks, and not in a good way. Los Angeles made the playoffs in both 2024 and 2025, and it was widely viewed as a contender entering the 2026 regular season.

However, the Chargers sit at 0-2 after dropping games to the Arizona Cardinals and Raiders. With a brutal schedule upcoming, it's hard to envision Los Angeles turning things around quickly.

L.A.'s next seven games are against teams that made the 2025 postseason.

Edge-rusher Khalil Mack will be a logical trade chip if the Chargers slide out of contention. He's 35, is playing on a one-year deal, and is still valuable as a rotational pass-rusher.

Mack has recorded a sack, two tackles for loss, and four quarterback pressures this season.

Potential Suitors: Chicago Bears, Detroit Lions

5. Mason Rudolph, QB, Pittsburgh Steelers

Projected Trade Value: Conditional 2027 6th-Round Pick

In a league filled with healthy quarterbacks, Pittsburgh Steelers backup Mason Rudolph would likely have minimal trade value. The 31-year-old does have 19 regular-season starts and one playoff start on his resume, but he's one of three understudies on Pittsburgh's roster behind Aaron Rodgers.

The Steelers also have rookie Drew Allar and second-year quarterback Will Howard in their QB room. According to NFL reporter Jason La Canfora, they've been open to moving Rudolph if they can find an interested team.

"The one thing stopping this is not Pittsburgh's willingness to sell, it's the number of quarterbacks potentially available across the league which could make finding a deal more difficult," La Canfora wrote for Casino.org.

With quarterback injuries mounting around the NFL, Pittsburgh might get the opportunity to get something in return for Rudolph. The list of Week 1 starters we've seen injured now includes Sam Darnold, Jayden Daniels, Jaxson Dart, and Caleb Williams.

Potential Suitors: Chicago Bears, New York Giants

The Miami Dolphins haven't looked very competitive through the first two weeks of the season, which is pretty much what was expected of them. Miami jettisoned most of its high-profile players in the offseason and focused on adding younger talent.

The Dolphins' focus in 2026 should be on evaluating players like 27-year-old quarterback Malik Willis, second-year guard Jonah Savaiinaea, and rookie tackle Kadyn Proctor. At some point, they should consider moving more veterans and fully embracing the youth movement.

Edge-defender Josh Uche just turned 28 and is one of the veteran leaders on Miami's defense. However, he's also set to be a free agent in the spring and should draw interest from contenders in need of pass-rushing help on the trade market.

Uche has played 51 percent of Miami's defensive snaps this season and has recorded 10 tackles and one tackle for loss.

Potential Suitors: Baltimore Ravens, Green Bay Packers

3. Kayvon Thibodeaux, Edge, New York Giants

Projected Trade Value: Conditional 2027 3rd-Round Pick

According to Dan Duggan of The Athletic, the New York Giants spoke with the New Orleans Saints about trading edge-rusher Kayvon Thibodeaux during the draft, though their asking price of a second-round pick was too high for the Saints.

With the Giants' season now in jeopardy, New York may make another run at moving the 25-year-old former first-round pick.

The Giants looked like a potential playoff team in their Week 1 win over the Dallas Cowboys. However, they fell flat against the Los Angeles Rams on Monday night, and they lost second-year quarterback Jaxson Dart to what may be a significant knee injury.

According to Rapoport and Mike Garafolo of NFL Network, Dart "will miss an extended period of time and is facing the possibility of season-ending surgery."

Thibodeaux was the fifth overall pick in 2022 and has flashed some elite upside during his time in New York. However, he's set to be a free agent in 2027. If the Giants aren't sold on keeping him and don't believe they can consistently win without Dart, now is the time to move Thibodeaux.

Potential Suitors: Detroit Lions, New Orleans Saints

In Week 2, the Cleveland Browns secure an upset road win over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. There's a chance that Cleveland isn't going to be the disaster of a team this season that it appeared to be in Week 1.

However, the Browns may still be motivated to move wide receiver Jerry Jeudy ahead of the trade deadline. The 2024 Pro Bowler spent his first two seasons in Cleveland as the team's No. 1 receiver, but it's clear that he's sliding down the hierarchy.

Rookie Denzel Boston, who caught seven passes for 154 yards and two touchdowns over the first two weeks, is the Browns' new No. 1 receiver. Fellow rookie KC Concepcion (10 catches, 71 yards) is the clear second option. Jeudy has become more of an offensive afterthought and saw just one target and no receptions in Week 2.

Jeudy has been a quality receiver in the past, and his 2026 base salary of $1.5 million should appeal to contenders in need of receiver help.

Potential Suitors: Houston Texans, Indianapolis Colts

Projected Trade Value: Conditional 2027 2nd-Round Pick

The San Francisco 49ers have looked like the best team in football through the first two weeks. As long as they view themselves as top Super Bowl contenders, they probably won't be eager to move one of the league's best backups, Mac Jones.

However, the 49ers have at least entertained the idea of trading Brock Purdy's top understudy. The Athletic's Zack Rosenblatt reported that San Francisco was looking for a second-round pick in exchange for Jones back in the spring.

Jones went 5-3 as a starter while throwing for 2,151 yards, 13 touchdowns and six interceptions in 2025. He's a terrific insurance policy for a team with championship aspirations, but he's also set to be a 2027 free agent. He's almost certain to depart for a starting opportunity next year, and at some point, offers for Jones may be too great to ignore.

We've already seen a handful of starters go down with significant injuries, and there's a good chance we'll see more before the trade deadline. If the 49ers can leverage multiple suitors against one another, they might even be able to come away from a trade with an extra first-round pick.

Potential Suitors: Atlanta Falcons, Washington Commanders

*Contract and cap information via Spotrac . Advanced statistics from Pro Football Reference .

articles.title: 4 Cleveland Browns Players We'd Like to See Get More Snaps Early in 2026
articles.summary: The Cleveland Browns enter Week 3 as a team still out to prove itself in the dawn of the Todd Monken era.
articles.body:
The Cleveland Browns enter Week 3 as a team still out to prove itself in the dawn of the Todd Monken era.

Things are looking a little more optimistic after beating the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on the road to get to 1-1. However, there are still a lot of players who are fighting to define their role and prove they should be part of the long-term vision.

No one is going to argue that the Browns are a playoff contender based on a win in Week 2. At least, they shouldn't. This is still shaping up to be a year that's more about evaluation than competition.

With that in mind, there are a few players that it would be nice to see more of in the coming weeks. Cleveland is a young team that has to figure out who it is and all four of these players on their rookie deal should get a bigger opportunity as the season progresses.

All snap count and advanced stats via Pro Football Reference unless otherwise noted.

Snaps: 7 in Week 1 (14 percent), 4 in Week 2 (7 percent)

The second-year speedster hasn't had many opportunities to show what he can do to this point. He's only played 11 total snaps, catching one target for 10 yards.

Simply put, Bond on the field does more for the offense than Jerry Jeudy at this point.

Through two games, the veteran wide receiver has been on field for 66 snaps and he has just five targets. He caught two of his four in Week 1 for 26 yards. However, he only had one ball come his way in the Week 2 victory.

Bond is not a natural X receiver in the same way that Jeudy is. Playing Bond more would mean more reps at the X for Denzel Boston. That's not a bad thing.

One thing Bond does offer is speed. He ran a 4.39 40 at the combine with decent ball-tracking skills to make plays over top.

He doesn't even have to make that money plays when he's on the field. Just having a speed threat with that kind of juice will open even more opportunities for Denzel Boston and KC Concepcion to make more plays.

Snaps: 0 in Week 1 (0 percent), 2 in Week 2 (3.4 percent)

Nothing. Jones has been relegated to being Tytus Howard's backup to this point. He went in for two snaps in the Week 2 loss, but that was just for Howard to get looked at after suffering a minor injury.

Because Tytus Howard has not looked good through the first two weeks of the season. The idea behind adding the veteran tackle was raising the floor for the position. As it turns out, the floor is still pretty low with how Howard is playing.

He has already accounted for a false start in each of the two games he has played. He was beaten for a sack in Week 2 against Tampa Bay and has graded out as the 58th tackle of the 66 PFF has graded to this point.

Jones might not do better. He has never completed a full season healthy and the last time he was a full-time starter for anything close to a season he gave up six sacks .

The difference is that there's at least some upside in playing Jones. His massive frame has always given him intriguing upside and it's hard to believe that he would be a downgrade from the version of Howard that played the first two games.

Snaps: 29 in Week 1 (51 percent), 26 in Week 2 (40 percent)

Hall is currently part of the defensive line rotation, but you wouldn't tell it from the box score. He played over half of the snaps in Week 1 and a slightly smaller workload in Week 2, but he has yet to register a tackle, sack or even a quarterback hit.

That all sounds like a reason that Hall should be playing less, but if you watch the film a different story emerges. LeCharles Bentley highlighted plenty of positives from Hall's game against the Buccaneers in his film breakdown.

The former Browns center called Hall, "the most disruptive interior DL on the Browns right now."

Among the clips he showed were an example of Hall being out of his stance before the rest of the entire defensive line and the third-year player blowing up a double team on inside zone to destroy the play.

Given Hall's explosiveness and what he has shown through the first two weeks, the numbers will come.

For now, he should be playing even more snaps as he continues to give offensive linemen fits and bring juice to the front seven.

Snaps: 14 in Week 1 (24.6 percent), 10 in Week 2 (15.4 percent)

McNeil-Warren has gotten in on some of the action. He played nearly a quarter of the reps in Week 1. Most of those were lined up as a deep safety, but he came down and played in the box a little as well. Week 2 saw him play a slightly smaller share of the snaps.

In those 24 defensive snaps (and 29 special teams snaps) he has six tackles.

Grant Delpit has played every snap of defense through two weeks and Ronnie Hickman isn't far behind him. McNeil-Warren has only worked as the third safety thus far.

The second-round pick should be given more opportunity to show what he can do.

McNeil-Warren is a versatile defender. The Browns clearly like him most as a deep safety, but he's also proven that he can come down and fill as a run defender as well.

It wouldn't hurt the Browns to reduce Hickman's role in the coming weeks and let the rookie play beside Delpit. Hickman already has two missed tackles and a touchdown conceded in coverage this season.

Meanwhile, McNeil-Warren has proven to be a physical defender with no missed tackles to this point. It's time to play him more and see if he can hold his own in coverage.

articles.title: B/R's Week 3 PPR Fantasy Football 2026 Player Rankings
articles.summary: In Week 1, we saw a barrage of scoring the likes of which the NFL has never seen in Week 1. There was scoring galore—and points on the board means points for fantasy managers.
articles.body:
In Week 1, we saw a barrage of scoring the likes of which the NFL has never seen in Week 1. There was scoring galore—and points on the board means points for fantasy managers.

However, we can't have nice things, so in Week 2 points were passe. And injuries were all the rage.

The number of fantasy-relevant players who either missed Week 2 or went down during the weekend's action is as long as it is depressing. Holes were blasted in rosters all over the place. The joy and jubilation of the opening week was replaced by doom and despair.

With that said, part of success in fantasy football is overcoming adversity. Rolling with the proverbial punches. We have to keep on keeping on and fight through the trials and tribulations that have been so cruelly thrust upon us.

That's what we're here to do—with tiered PPR Rankings, player commentary and advice and the top-125 players overall for Week 3.

In what is sadly going to be a theme this week, there were multiple fantasy-relevant injuries at the quarterback position in Week 2—injuries that affect not just the quarterback rankings but the entire fantasy landscape.

In Chicago, Caleb Williams went down in the fourth quarter of Sunday's loss to the Minnesota Vikings with what appeared at first to be an ugly-looking injury. But despite being carted off the field, Williams avoided serious injury—he's week to week after pulling his hamstring.

Two NFC East quarterbacks weren't as fortunate. Jayden Daniels of the Washington Commanders dislocated his elbow on the final play of the first half in Dallas, while Jaxson Dart of the New York Giants suffered a potentially season-ending knee injury in Monday's loss to the Los Angeles Rams.

Both will be out indefinitely and are likely headed to injured reserve.

A trio of high-end, set and forget weekly starters. Josh Allen of the Buffalo Bills in particular is on a rampage to begin the season—after scoring five total touchdowns in Week 2 against the Detroit Lions, Allen has eclipsed 35 fantasy points in both of his starts this year.

The Tier 2 quarterbacks in Week 3 might not be elite, but they can be started with confidence. Patrick Mahomes of the Chiefs looked like his old self in torching the Indianapolis Colts for 382 passing yards and three scores Sunday night, while Brock Purdy of the San Francisco 49ers has quietly been a top-five fantasy option in the early-going.

The confidence level drops a bit once you hit the Tier 3 quarterbacks, but there's upside to go with that uncertainty. Jared Goff of the Detroit Lions is coming off a four-touchdown effort in last week's loss to the Bills. Trevor Lawrence of the Jacksonville Jaguars had a similarly productive effort in his last home start.

With all the injuries at quarterback, there will be fantasy managers starting Tier 4 quarterbacks whether they want to or not. Bryce Young of the Carolina Panthers is off to the best start of his NFL career, with three touchdown passes in both games. Geno Smith of the New York Jets faces a Detroit Lions defense that has been abysmal so far this year.

There will be more Tier 5 quarterbacks in lineups this week than we'd like, but so it goes with all the injuries at the position. C.J. Stroud of the Houston Texans takes on an Indianapolis Colts team surrendering the most fantasy points in the AFC to quarterbacks, and Sam Darnold of the Seahawks is expected to return to the lineup this week against a struggling Washington Commanders defense.

Unless you are playing in a "Superflex" or two-QB leagues, fantasy managers should want no part of the quarterbacks in Tier 6. It's a motley arrangement of backups thrust into the starting lineup by injuries and a player in Atlanta's Michael Penix who is coming off a season-ending ACL tear.

There were a couple of injuries at the running back position last week (Rico Dowdle of the Pittsburgh Steelers and JK Dobbins of the Denver Broncos), but we'll take a break from the depressing stuff and accentuate the positive.

Kenneth Walker III of the Kansas City Chiefs is positively on a rampage over his first two games in Kansas City.

Fantasy football's highest scoring running back after two weeks has become the focal point of the Chiefs offense—and he's loving every minute of it. Walker is averaging over six yards per carry and 145 rushing yards per game. He leads the NFL in touches (56) and total yards (369) and has found the end zone twice.

Until further notice, Walker is a locked-in top-five fantasy option.

This may be as deep as we'll see the top tier at running back, but all of these ball-carriers are bellcows in both the NFL and fantasy. All six backs in tier 1 rank in the top-10 in PPR points after two weeks. All six should see 20-plus touches. And all six are every-week starts so long as they are healthy.

The second tier of running backs isn't quite as beastly as the first one, but each has the potential for a top-five week. Monitor the health of Saquon Barkley of the Eagles, who missed a chunk of last week's win over the Tennessee Titans with a stinger. Outside that, roll this group out with a smile on your face.

There's plenty of upside present with these fantasy RB2, but there's also the potential for disappointment. Omarion Hampton of the Chargers and De'Von Achane of the Dolphins have struggled to get untracked on bad offenses, while Cam Skattebo of the Giants is going to see a lot of stacked boxes with Jaxson Dart on the shelf.

Tier 4 is the maybe brigade—a group of running backs with significant question marks. Can Jaylen Warren of the Steelers take advantage of the added workload he'll see against Cincinnati if Rico Dowdle can't go? Can Quinshon Judkins and the Browns run game finally get going in the home opener against the Panthers?

The "star" of Tier 5 is rookie Jonah Coleman of the Broncos, who could be at the very least Denver's early-down back in Week 3 with Dobbins likely to sit or even an every-down back if R.J. Harvey's hamstring sidelines him another week. However, the sledding isn't going to be easy against a stout Rams defense.

This tier is a group of complimentary backs for whom the biggest issue is simple—touches. Emmanuel Wilson of the Seahawks could see heavy usage again with Jadarian Price (chest) banged up. The Chiefs have talked about using rookie Emmett Johnson more to lessen Kenneth Walker's workload with long-term success in mind.

For the final tier of Week 3 running backs to have even flex value, something either has to go sideways on the depth chart ahead of them or they need to score a fluky touchdown. These backs are bench depth and bye week fill-ins—nothing more.

Fantasy managers were hit hard by injuries at wide receiver in Week 2—multiple big names (Houston's Nico Collins, Puka Nacua of the Rams and Baltimore's Zay Flowers among them) were sidelined, and more pass-catchers (Buffalo's D.J. Moore and Alec Pierce of the Colts) joined them on the shelf.

It wasn't all doom and gloom, though. A pair of NFC West wideouts went ballistic in Week 3—Seattle's Jaxson Smith-Njigba and Davante Adams of the Rams combined for 350 receiving yards, five touchdowns and approximately all the PPR points ever.

If you were short-handed at the position and faced one of those monsters in Week 2, you have my sympathies.

Smith-Njigba and Adams weren't the only wideouts who went into Godzilla mode in Week 2—Amon-Ra St. Brown of the Lions caught nine passes for 142 yards and two scores against the Buffalo Bills. Minnesota's Justin Jefferson should rebound in Week 3—unless there's another typhoon in Tampa on Sunday.

The second tier of wide receivers all have relatively high floors to go along with a top-five fantasy ceiling. Parker Washington of the Jaguars has emerged as Jacksonville's clear No. 1 receiver, while Garrett Wilson of the Jets is clicking with Geno Smith and draws a great matchup this week with Detroit's non-existent defense.

Tier 3 consists of solid second starters or players with top-12 potential but some form of question mark. Monitor Flowers' practice participation, although there's early optimism he'll be able to return this week against the Cowboys. Christian Watson of the Packers is off to an excellent start to the season—he's found the end zone three times already.

This tier is a mixture of surprise stars and slow starters. Jalen Coker of the Panthers cooled off a little last week after a gonzo opener, but he still ranks among the top-10 receivers for the season. Emeka Egbuka of the Buccaneers, um, does not—with the Tampa passing game sputtering, Egbuka sits outside the top-30 receivers after two games.

We're still in weekly starter territory, but things are starting to get a little dicey by the time you hit Tier 5. Stefon Diggs is off to a hot start in Washington, but quarterback questions loom over him and batterymate Terry McLaurin. Chicago's Luther Burden has the same issue—Tyson Bagent doesn't inspire much in the way of fantasy confidence.

The sixth tier contains a pair of surprisingly productive youngsters in Adonai Mitchell of the Jets and Denzel Boston of the Browns (who has touchdowns in each of his first two NFL games. That duo has exceeded expectations (Mitchell had none), but rookie Carnell Tate has disappointed. With the Tennessee passing attack all but non-existent, Tate is WR58 in PPR points two weeks in.

That both DeVaughn Vele of the Saints and Tre Tucker of the Raiders are ranked ahead of Marvin Harrison Jr. of the Cardinals tells you everything you need to know about how Harrison's third season has started. Two weeks in, Harrison has all of one reception and has only been targeted four times. That's just icky.

There's a chance for some dart-throw success in the final tier of wide receivers—Kansas City's Xavier Worthy is a threat to score every time he touches the ball, and the Texans need to get Kayshon Boutte more involved in the offense. But these wide receivers are more likely score four PPR points in Week 3 than 14. Bench them if possible.

There's good news and bad news for fantasy managers at the tight end position in Week 3.

We'll do the bad news first, because that's what Week 2 was—bad news.

After catching two touchdown passes against the Commanders in Week 1, Dallas Goedert of the Eagles made it just one catch into Week 2 before going down with a knee injury. Goedert has been diagnosed with a sprained MCL and could be a candidate for short-term injured reserve.

The good news is that Brock Bowers of the Raiders appears headed toward his first game action of 2026—after sitting out the first two weeks following knee surgery, Bowers will reportedly practice this week and should be good to go for this week's trip to New Orleans.

The fantasy gods giveth, and the fantasy gods taketh away.

There's not a lot to say about the top "tier" of tight ends—Arizona's Trey McBride has been targeted 23 times and leads all tight ends in PPR points. A healthy Bowers could crash this party, but for now at least McBride is in a class by himself.

The second tier of tight ends aren't the relatively sure bet that McBride is, but one hasn't been far off—after 12 catches for 225 yards and a touchdown over his first two games, Dalton Kincaid of the Bills is hot on McBride's heels, Travis Kelce of the Chiefs has also come out of the gate hot, including nice catches for 101 yards and a score last week against the Colts.

By the time you hit the back end of Tier 3, upside starts giving way to uncertainty. The upside is with guys like Houston's Dalton Schultz, who had a huge Week 2 with Nico Collins sidelined in Week 2. The uncertainty is rampant with Kyle Pitts of the Falcons, who has been on a milk carton thanks to the horrendous quarterback play in Atlanta this season.

There is some potential for a solid stat line from the Tier 4 tight ends—Juwan Johnson of the Saints has quietly posted double-digit PPR points in both of his games this season. Mark Andrews of the Ravens narrowly missed duplicating that feat, but he has yet to find the end zone in 2026.

Tier 5 is for fans of 301—because the tight ends in it are dart throws. Terrance Ferguson of the Rams caught his first touchdown pass of the season Monday against the Giants, and Orande Gadsden of the Chargers will see a larger offensive role after David Njoku broke his leg. But target share with this bench is a real issue—they could see two looks as easily as six.

Unless you play in a league that requires multiple starters at tight end or you're in a deep league and have been bitten by the injury bug, the final tier of tight ends is best left on benches and waiver wires. The only real path to fantasy relevance for this bunch lies in reeling in a touchdown, and that's not especially likely.

One of the reasons why it's generally advisable not to invest in a high-end fantasy defense is that so much can change from year to year. Trash becomes treasure and vice-versa.

The treasure has been the Cincinnati Bengals—that is not a misprint. After dominating the Houston Texans in Week 2, a Bengals defense that was among the NFL's worst in 2025 has more fantasy points than any team in the league. They are piling up big plays—and big plays equal fantasy points.

The trash is the aforementioned Texans. Last year, no team in the AFC had more fantasy points than Houston, and the Texans were one of the first defenses drafted in 2026. But thanks in part to a pair of bad matchups with the Bills and Bengals, the Houston defense sits outside the top-20 in fantasy points after two weeks.

Success in fantasy where defenses are concerned is all about the matchups—and the Tier 1 defenses all have great ones this week. The Seahawks face the reeling Commanders after dominating Arizona. The Chiefs face the league's worst team in the Dolphins. The Eagles take on Tyson Bagent and Da Bears. Tasty.

It's put up or shut up time for the aforementioned Houston Texans—it's going to be hard to justify rostering them in fantasy if the team posts a third straight clunker. The Los Angeles Rams and Denver Broncos are both talented defenses who were drafted early over the summer, but they face one another on Sunday night at Mile High.

By Tier 3, we're already into the matchup dart throws and "name" defenses that have underperformed and/or have poor Week 3 matchups. The Carolina Panthers have one awful defensive outing this year and one huge stat line—they face a Browns team that allowed the second-most fantasy points to defenses in 2025.

There are three defenses in fantasy who have scored double-digit fantasy points in both games this season—and one of those defenses is the Las Vegas Raiders. The New Orleans Saints are far better offensively in 2026 than a year ago, but the Raiders are an OK Hail Mary play off the waiver wire.

The fifth tier of defenses is the 10-foot pole club—as in don't touch them with one. It's a group of bad defenses, worse matchups or a combination of both. Leave them on the waiver wire where they belong.

Want to know why fantasy managers should never, ever draft a kicker before the last round? Take a look at the top-five at the position after two weeks.

Evan McPherson of the Bengals is pacing the position in the early-going. He is followed by Chase McLaughlin of the Buccaneers, Harrison Butker of the Chiefs, Trey Smack of the Green Bay Packers and Spencer Shrader of the Colts.

The majority of those kickers weren't drafted at all. I'm not even sure Trey Smack is a real person. It sounds made-up.

That list will undoubtedly change. But it goes to show that there's no point in spending draft capital on a kicker when high-end options are available for free well into the regular season.

Brandon Aubrey of the Cowboys and Cam Little of the Jaguars play for teams with potent offenses and have huge legs (figuratively speaking). Jason Myers of the Seahawks has long been a consistently productive fantasy option. The 49ers offense is rolling right now, so Eddy Piniero cracks this week's top-five.

The aforementioned Evan McPherson and Harrison Butker are Tier 2 kickers this week—solid weekly starters. Baltimore's Tyler Loop should rebound this week against a leaky Cowboys defense. Pittsburgh's Chris Boswell should be busy in Week 3—the Steelers are apparently allergic to touchdowns.

This week's third tier of kickers is a spinning wheel of maybes in Week 3. Smack may do nothing but kick extra points against the woeful Falcons. The same goes for Buffalo's Tyler Bass—the Bills don't stop until they hit the paint. There could be a top-five option in this tier—and multiple disappointments.

Unless your fantasy league requires multiple kickers, the back end of the kicker rankings is a hard pass. If your league does require multiple kickers, then seek help immediately—you're an even bigger fantasy football degenerate than this idiot.

Before we help you make "Flex" lineup decisions for Week 3 with the Top 125 players overall, it's time for weekly notes.

The first is the same as always—there are no quarterbacks on this list. The injuries at the position have reduced the number of viable guys for "Superflex" starts this week, but if you do have a decent QB2 he should get the nod in that format.

The second is a refrain I make often at this time of year—chill. I'm well aware that starting season 0-2 isn't ideal. I draft a team live for the King's Classic at the Pro Football Hall of Fame each year. My team there is winless. My starting quarterback is dead. My IR slots are all filled two weeks in. I have said many bad words.

But freaking out won't help get me to 1-2. And that's the only concern right now. Making the team better where possible and notching that first win. 0-2 can become 2-2 quickly. So stay the course. Shake off the injuries. Hit the waiver wire.

Gary Davenport is a two-time Fantasy Sports Writers Association Football Writer of the Year. Follow Gary on X at @IDPGodfather .

articles.title: NFL Brazil 2026: Funk, favelas and football - what to expect as Baltimore Ravens face Dallas Cowboys in league's Rio de Janeiro debut
articles.summary: The NFL will play its first regular-season game in Rio de Janeiro as the Baltimore Ravens face the Dallas Cowboys at the Maracana Stadium, live on Sky Sports from 9.25pm Sunday; NFL Brazil General Manager Luis Martinez promises a "unique experience" on the league's return to South America
articles.body:
By now the league has discovered that a permit to party knows no meaning of expiration in the carnival epicentre of the world, for New York has met its sleepless match, and so too aspiring-come-rivalling NFL host cities across the globe.

A footballing bloco that has spent the last two years step-ball-changing in Sao Paulo this week reaches the sandy collars of Rio, where the iconic Maracana Stadium will host Lamar Jackson's Ravens and Dak Prescott's Cowboys in its first-ever NFL regular-season matchup.

"Brazil is an amazing, amazing, amazing country, and the territory, the Brazilians, these vibrant, unique opportunities with food, carnival samba and experiences that are super unique in Brazil I would recommend everyone to live them at least once," NFL Brazil general manager Luis Martinez tells Sky Sports.

Soccer reigns as the unconquerable sporting religion to Rio. Where murals of Neymar and Vinicius Jr dress up the walls of favelas, where children welcome tourists to play football in FIFA Street-style courts. Ronaldinho and Ronaldo shirts line the walkways of Copacabana and Ipanema beaches, on the sandy canvas of which locals commonly deliver a masterclass in keepy-ups. On any given gameday football is watched on television in barbers, coffee shops, restaurants, beachfront bars, convenience stores and, in this writer's case, the digital screen of my Argentina-despising Uber driver.

But the belief is that footballing obsession breeds sporting obsession.

"Yes it is a soccer-dominated market, we all know. It's crazy. Breakfast, lunch, and dinner, the only conversation is going to be soccer, but they are super open, and the fans we have for the NFL, they have really proven that," Martinez says.

"We have vibrant colours to explode that are amazing and very different than the way we have been doing things at the NFL and international. Food and samba, dance, caipirinhas, cantores, it's so unique.

"We have so many iconic elements, Christ the Redeemer, Pão de Açúcar (Sugarloaf Mountain), Copacabana, Ipanema, it's super diverse for the creative elements."

Rio features among a record slate of nine international games and as one of three new territories alongside Paris and Melbourne, the latter of which just played stage to the San Francisco 49ers against the Los Angeles Rams in front of 100,000 fans at the Melbourne Cricket Ground.

The NFL made its debut in Brazil, as well as South America, in September 2024 when the Green Bay Packers faced the Philadelphia Eagles at Sao Paulo's Corinthians Arena in the opening week of the season. It returned to the same venue the following year when the Los Angeles Chargers beat the Kansas City Chiefs, before the league announced a multi-year commitment to playing a minimum of three regular-season games over five years in Rio.

"Rio and Sao Paulo, completely different," said Martinez. "One is super, I could say, corporate and industrial, and the other one is chill and vibes. Havaianas everywhere, and coconut water, which is amazing.

"So once you understand the way you need to execute things in a different city, it's just a great magic, and that's what we are doing, and it's super exciting."

By the end of the 2026 season the NFL will have played 71 regular-season games outside of the US, dating back to the first in Mexico City in October 2005. From the Estadio Azteca to the Bernabeu, football has spanned some of the most iconic theatres in sport. It now adds another crowning jewel in the Maracana.

"I'm expecting to have the level of noise and volume from Cariocas and everyone attending to be the loudest and biggest from an international game," Martinez added. "For me it's literally a real authentic representation of every single element that we identify as a key priority, or as very relevant for a local carioca, that we are exploding, maximizing."

The NFL has seen it all. But never has it encountered such a chameleon city with the same infectious magnetism, from the natural beauty of its beaches and Tijuca National Park to its world wonder, rich sporting heritage and anti-Footloose dance obligation.

So often international games tell the story of more than simply the football, offering new corners of the world an opportunity to showcase the best of their personality and their DNA. Now, it is Rio's turn.

"We are trying to break a Guinness World Record with the biggest jersey on the sand, like a sculpture representing the Rio game," said Martinez. "We are doing cool surprises on Christ the Redeemer, we are maximising the most relevant and iconic places in the city.

"We are having a female under-15 flag football, adding two community events with both the Ravens and Cowboys. We are having watch parties and influencer activations including flag games.

"We are doing very carioca Rio things, like airplanes with messages, kind of cliche but that could be so amazing and unique for us as well to send messages into the air. We are doing activations on the lagoon as well, and for the third year we will have an NFL race, a family walk of 2km and then a 5km race."

Beyond the showpiece prestige of the game itself on Sunday is the bigger picture of a lasting and expanding legacy; football is here, but Rio and Brazil want to ensure it is here to stay.

"Crianças, or kids in English, are super relevant, because if they start and they engage with the NFL, they will be there forever, and the passion they have is very different than a natural fan that has been there, an avid fan that has been there forever," said Martinez.

"Our commitment to kids and community is through different pillars. The first one is the flag tournament. We have three national tournaments, with representation from all the regions in Brazil, under-15 female, under-14 co-ed, boys and girls, under 12-co-ed, boys and girls

"These three teams that will win these tournaments will represent Brazil. So we need this exposure, we need this visibility worldwide, not only in Latin America or America. Our ambition is to have a national school program so they can select flag in Brazil."

With the NFL's arrival and football's growth comes another avenue to connect with children based in Rio's favelas, which typically represent the city's most impoverished communities.

"In the first two years we have had representation from favelas in the actual tournament," Martinez explained. "It's very different because that is part of the magic as well. You saw Corinthians club kids that are super immersed in the game versus kids coming from the favela who are probably leaving the favela for the first time ever, imagine the experience.

"It's something that is super rewarding, personally and professionally. Imagine changing your day-to-day for the first time ever, but going somewhere and seeing or meeting an NFL player, or cheerleaders and mascots, and the whole experience.

"Our intention is to continue growing and negotiating with these favela organisations, because honestly the talent we have found in favelas is so great for everything, like artists, music composers, graffiti artists, dancers, singers. We need to give voice to these communities, and that's part of our job."

The Cowboys (1-1) arrive on the back of a 37-20 victory over the Washington Commanders, during which Prescott threw four touchdown passes to surpass Tony Romo for the all-time franchise record. Behind CeeDee Lamb, George Pickens and Jake Ferguson, Dallas boast one of football's most high-powered aerial attacks, which averaged the second most yards in the league last season.

Baltimore (1-1) are meanwhile coming off a 24-17 defeat to the New Orleans Saints after blowing an eight-point fourth-quarter lead. The Ravens entered the season with soaring expectations following the appointment of first-year head coach Jesse Minter, who replaced John Harbaugh after 18 seasons tasked with cashing in on the prime of quarterback Lamar Jackson. The two-time league MVP has been knocking on the Super Bowl door with three Divisional Round exits and one AFC Championship Game defeat since 2019, his Ravens missing out on the playoffs with an 8-9 record as one of the disappointments of last season.

Rio de Janeiro welcomes two contenders to town, where caipirinhas meet catches, where tapioca meets tackles, where samba meets sacks, where favelas meet a new brand football.

Monday: Rio's famed Pedra do Sal street party. Tuesday: Sugarloaf Mountain's sunset DJ. Wednesday: A visit to Christ the Redeemer. Thursday: A hike through Tijuca National Park. Friday: A night in Lapa. Saturday: Samba dos Guimarães in Santa Teresa. Sunday: NFL history. Quite the addition your typical unrelenting Rio week.

articles.title: In 2018, NFL star Von Miller turned his passion for poultry into a 35-acre Texas farm; years later, his Greener Pastures operation was growing into a major organic chicken business
articles.summary: NFL News: Von Miller has always had two serious jobs. Most people only know about one of them. The Super Bowl 50 MVP and eight-time Pro Bowler launched Greener .
articles.body: Von Miller has always had two serious jobs. Most people only know about one of them. The Super Bowl 50 MVP and eight-time Pro Bowler launched Greener Pastures Chicken in Elgin, Texas, in 2018 alongside co-founder Cameron Molberg, and what began as a side passion has since grown into something the agriculture industry is paying close attention to. The 35-acre farm is now the first broiler operation in the United States to earn Regenerative Organic Certified status, a distinction no other chicken farm in the country holds. Miller's operation has attracted NFL investors, expanded into a USDA-certified organic processing facility, and recently locked up a $100,000 boost in school district revenue through the Texas Farm Fresh Network.How a Poultry science degree at Texas A&M became the foundation of a farming businessVon Miller grew up raising chickens in DeSoto, Texas, so the subject matter was never foreign to him. But when he enrolled in poultry science at Texas A&M, the honest truth is he wasn't trying to build a business empire. He was trying to keep his football GPA intact. The class, he later admitted, was meant to be an easy credit. It didn't go quite as planned.He fell asleep in lectures. Professors made him stand in front of the class and explain chicken husbandry from memory. Somehow, that cycle of embarrassment and repetition worked. By the time he was being picked second overall in the 2011 NFL Draft, he already knew how to talk about birds in ways most linemen couldn't. He named his Broncos teammates after the chickens he raised back home. Peyton. DT. DeMarcus. He told a television audience about it with the kind of casual pride most athletes reserve for playoff runs.The early version of his farming ambition was modest. In 2014, he purchased 38 chickens and began raising them on an eight-acre property near Dallas, calling it Miller Farms. At the time, some in the industry found it charming but didn't take it too seriously. "Miller Farms is where I'm starting out, but it's all raw right now," he said back then. "This is just a small investment where I can see where I go from here. Hopefully it will snowball into something bigger."It did.What makes Greener Pastures chicken different from every other organic farm in TexasThe farm operates out of Elgin, Texas, and it is built around a set of principles that separate it from most operations in the organic poultry space. For starters, Greener Pastures is the only farm in Texas that raises birds on grass while supplementing their diet with USDA Certified Organic feed. The chickens live outside. Full access to sunshine, fresh air, native grasses, and whatever bugs they find foraging. Mobile coops are moved regularly so the soil isn't depleted, which is a core practice in regenerative agriculture.That rotational grazing model is part of why the farm holds its Regenerative Organic Certified designation, the first broiler farm in the entire country to earn it. The operation adds between a quarter and a half inch of healthy soil back to the land each year. That's not a marketing tagline. That's measurable ecological output. The Regenerative Organic Alliance, the body that issues the certification, focuses on soil health, animal welfare, feed inputs, and social fairness standards, all of which Greener Pastures meets.Molberg, the co-founder who runs day-to-day farm operations, brings over 15 years of experience in organic agriculture to the operation. He is described by peers as an "encyclopedia in blue jeans," someone other farmers and organizations call when they need to understand regenerative systems at a practical level. The two make for a complementary partnership. Miller brings the platform, the capital, and frankly the story. Molberg brings the institutional knowledge to make the farm function at a high level.The processing plant opening that went almost completely under the radarIn April 2024, Von Miller cut the ribbon on a brand new processing facility in Elgin, Texas, joined by Greener Pastures staff and faculty from the Texas A&M Department of Poultry Science. The facility is the first USDA organic poultry processing plant in the state of Texas. That is a significant milestone for the industry, not just for Miller personally. And yet there was no splashy press release, no major media rollout.The Texas A&M poultry science department shared the news on LinkedIn, and the industry trade press picked it up from there. A Super Bowl MVP opening the first USDA organic poultry processing facility in a state as large as Texas is exactly the kind of story that should generate national coverage. The fact that it didn't, and that Miller didn't push hard to make it happen, says something about how he has chosen to build this business. Quietly, methodically, and with more concern for the product than the profile.The LinkedIn post from the university read in part: "Von Miller is known to have two great passions in life, football and chicken. Greener Pastures Chicken reflects Von's dedication to producing a humane and sustainable product." The processing facility represents the kind of vertical integration that makes a farm operation genuinely scalable, controlling output from pasture to processing to retail shelf.Why Patrick Mahomes and Drew Brees bought into Von Miller's chicken companyMiller spent years building the farm before he ever pitched it to anyone in the NFL. That approach, building proof before seeking investors, is what made the pitch easy when he finally made it. Patrick Mahomes and Drew Brees are now among the NFL investors who have backed Greener Pastures Chicken, according to the Entrepreneur podcast where Miller discussed the company's growth in August 2025.The investor circle has since expanded further into the locker room. When Miller joined the Dallas Cowboys for the 2026 NFL season, he negotiated his preferred jersey number, No. 40, from Cowboys fullback Hunter Luepke in a way that made national sports news for all the right reasons. Instead of cash, he offered Luepke equity in Greener Pastures Chicken."It was great. You got to give Hunter a great shoutout. He's learned from the best negotiators here with the Cowboys," Miller said. "I'm happy to say he's my business partner. He's a part owner of Greener Pastures Chicken. The chicken of champions."The "chicken of champions" line sounds like a slogan, but it carries real weight when you consider the athletes who have bought in. Luepke won multiple college national championships before the NFL, which Miller cited as part of the brand connection. The jersey deal was described as one of the most unique number negotiations in NFL history, swapping traditional compensation for actual business ownership.How Greener Pastures grew its revenue through Texas school districtsThe farm's growth has moved beyond specialty retail. Through Texas Agriculture Commissioner Sid Miller's Farm Fresh Network, Greener Pastures formed new partnerships with local school districts, adding $100,000 in expanded sales revenue. That shift from co-op shelves to school lunch programs is not a small step. Institutional purchasing brings volume, consistency, and a meaningful mission dimension to the operation."Joining the Farm Fresh Network isn't just about recognition; it opens doors and opportunities that wouldn't have been possible otherwise," said Diego Diverde, Sales Director at Greener Pastures.In Austin's retail market, the brand is already stocked at Central Market, Wheatsville Co-Op, and Radius Butcher and Grocery, three premium food destinations with customer bases that take sourcing seriously. The farm has also signed the Better Chicken Commitment, holds Certified Humane certification, and meets stocking density and enrichment standards that go well beyond what standard organic labeling requires.In 2025, Greener Pastures also adopted the USDA's voluntary "Product of USA" label, a designation that confirms poultry was born, raised, processed, and packaged entirely within the United States. It is the kind of certification that resonates with a consumer market that has grown increasingly attentive to supply chain transparency.What Von Miller's farm business says about NFL athletes and life after footballThe story of athletes going broke after football is a well-documented one. Miller represents something different, an athlete who used his education, not just his earnings, to build something durable. He took poultry science at Texas A&M because it seemed easy. He ended up building the only Regenerative Organic Certified broiler farm in America.That arc, from dozing off in an agriculture lecture to cutting the ribbon on a USDA organic processing facility, is not a straight line. It took over a decade of patient construction. He started with 38 birds. He built proof before he built buzz. He let the farm develop credibility before he attached his jersey number negotiations to it. Now he is describing it publicly as "the chicken of champions" with the kind of genuine confidence that only comes from having done the actual work.There is also a broader question of what this model means for sustainable agriculture. Greener Pastures is not just a celebrity vanity project. It holds real certifications, sells through real retail and institutional channels, runs a processing facility with USDA oversight, and is actively contributing to soil regeneration on Texas land. The Cornucopia Institute, a watchdog organization that evaluates organic farms, has rated Greener Pastures highly, noting that Cameron Molberg, who also serves as the organization's board chair, did not influence the review process.Miller has talked openly about where he sees the farm heading by 2030, without specifying the exact targets publicly. What is already clear is that the operation is structurally serious. A processing plant, school district contracts, NFL co-investors, Regenerative Organic Certification, and a USDA Product of USA designation are not things you build by accident. articles.body: Russell Wilson has found a way to make a lasting mark off the football field, and his latest success story comes in a surprising size. Their company, 3BRAND, has grown into a major part of Wilson's business portfolio, showing how a family-inspired venture can find room in a competitive market. With a Nike collaboration and strong sales, the brand is gaining attention beyond the NFL.Russell Wilson's 3BRAND turns a family idea into a $100 million businessThe idea behind 3BRAND came from Wilson and Ciara's own family. Its moisture-wicking shirts and workout clothes have helped it carve out space in a retail market filled with established sportswear giants.The numbers tell a striking story. 3BRAND generated more than $100 million in sales in 2024. articles.title: Travis Kelce Reacts to Taylor Swift Memes After Viral Video of Celebration Showing Off Wedding Ring
articles.summary: Even though the Kansas City Chiefs are off to a 2-0 start after a dramatic overtime win in Week 2 over the Indianapolis Colts, clearly the biggest story coming out of the game was Taylor Swift's reaction to Travis Kelce's touchdown catch.
articles.body:
Even though the Kansas City Chiefs are off to a 2-0 start after a dramatic overtime win in Week 2 over the Indianapolis Colts, clearly the biggest story coming out of the game was Taylor Swift's reaction to Travis Kelce's touchdown catch.

On the latest episode of the New Heights podcast (starts at 17:35 mark), Travis and Jason Kelce reacted to the viral memes that stemmed from Swift pointing at her wedding ring in celebration of Travis' first-quarter score.

"The internet's having a good old time with this s--t," Travis said as he was reading some of the memes. "... Listen, man, proud wife, baby. I gotta make my girl proud."

Swift created the instant viral moment when Kelce caught a 13-yard touchdown pass from Patrick Mahomes to put the Chiefs up 10-7.

Here are some of the social-media responses that the Kelce brothers specifically called out.

Kelce and Swift got married on July 3 at a ceremony held inside Madison Square Garden. The singer-songwriter has been at each of the Chiefs' first two games this season to cheer on her new husband.

Swift has also been keeping busy with her day job, announcing on Tuesday she will be releasing a new single later this week. It is his first new material since the couple wed.

Kelce, now in his 14th season, is off to a strong start through two games. He has 12 receptions for 172 yards and one touchdown. Sunday's game marked his first 100-yard performance in the regular season since Week 9 of the 2024 season.

articles.title: Jonathon Brooks Injured, Latest Updates, Timeline for Panthers RB's Return After Surgery
articles.summary: The Carolina Panthers placed running back Jonathon Brooks on injured reserve Wednesday, meaning he will have to miss at least the next four games.
articles.body:
The Carolina Panthers placed running back Jonathon Brooks on injured reserve Wednesday, meaning he will have to miss at least the next four games.

However, according to NFL Network's Ian Rapoport , Brooks' absence will extend even longer than the minimum four games, as he is expected to miss at least the next six games after undergoing core muscle surgery.

NFL insider Jordan Schultz followed up by reporting that the Panthers are bringing in veteran free-agent running back Austin Ekeler for a visit Wednesday, as they search for some potential depth behind RB1 Chuba Hubbard.

After a strong collegiate career at the University of Texas, Brooks was the first running back selected in the 2024 NFL draft, as the Panthers took him 46th overall in the second round.

It was widely expected that Brooks would be the Panthers' starting running back of the future, but that has yet to come to fruition due to a multitude of injuries.

Brooks played only three games as a rookie, as he spent much of the season rehabbing a torn ACL suffered in college before tearing his ACL again just a few games into his NFL career.

The Panthers then held Brooks out for the entire 2025 campaign so he could recover from the second successive ACL tear.

With the 23-year-old Brooks seeming to be largely healthy during training camp this year, he once again became a trendy pick to lead the Panthers' backfield and break out.

Because of that, he was a popular sleeper selection in fantasy football drafts, often being picked ahead of Hubbard.

Brooks had only 11 touches over the Panthers' first two games this season, though, rushing nine times for 30 yards and catching two passes for 43 yards.

Meanwhile, Hubbard cemented himself as the Panthers' starting running back once again, rushing 22 times for 102 yards and a touchdown, and catching five passes for 49 yards and two scores through two games.

Now that Brooks is once again set to miss an extended period of time, the backfield essentially belongs entirely to Hubbard in Carolina.

AJ Dillon is the only other running back on the Panthers' active roster right now, and while he had some success in the past, including averaging nearly 729 rushing yards per season with the Green Bay Packers from 2021 to 2023, he is a somewhat one-dimensional, between-the-tackles bruiser.

If the Panthers sign Ekeler, it will give them more versatility since he is a quality pass-catcher with 480 career receptions to his credit, but Ekeler and Dillon would likely only have specialized roles, while Hubbard continues to take the bulk of the snaps and opportunities.

articles.title: Patrick Mahomes' Play in Return From Injury Evaluated by NFL Exec, Chiefs QB 'Ripping the Ball'
articles.summary: Any questions about Patrick Mahomes' returning to his peak form coming off a torn ACL appear to have been put to rest based on how he has played through the first two weeks for the undefeated Kansas City Chiefs.
articles.body:
Any questions about Patrick Mahomes' returning to his peak form coming off a torn ACL appear to have been put to rest based on how he has played through the first two weeks for the undefeated Kansas City Chiefs.

Per ESPN's Jeremy Fowler , one NFL personnel evaluator described Mahomes as "ripping the ball" right now.

"His ability to drive throws — I thought he was ripping the ball," the evaluator said.

Fowler noted the general feeling about Mahomes throughout the league right now is that he may not be "all the way back" at this point, but "he's not far off."

There did look to be some rust in Week 1 against the Denver Broncos. Mahomes finished 15-of-27 for 184 yards, two touchdowns and one interception, but it didn't matter because the rushing attack and defense were so good they cruised to a 31-10 victory.

Sunday's 33-30 overtime win over the Indianapolis Colts looked much more like vintage Mahomes. He went 32-of-47 for 382 yards with three touchdowns and no interceptions.

It was Mahomes' first game with at least 350 passing yards and three touchdowns since Week 1 of the 2022 season when he had 360 yards and five touchdowns in a 44-21 win over the Arizona Cardinals.

The 2022 season was the last time Mahomes won the NFL MVP award. It's perhaps not a coincidence that was also their best rushing year in the previous four years by EPA ( 0.02 EPA per rush).

Adding Kenneth Walker III in the offseason has revitalized the Chiefs' ground game. He leads the NFL with 290 rushing yards, and the team is tied with the Baltimore Ravens for best EPA per rush (0.17) through two weeks.

Having a running game that opposing defenses have to respect makes life so much easier for Mahomes. He has taken advantage of it thus far and making the Chiefs look like they are once again a Super Bowl contender in the AFC.

articles.title: Travis Kelce Sounds Off on Colts' Cam Bynum Not Knowing OT Coin Toss Rules in Chiefs' Win
articles.summary: Kansas City Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce addressed the confusion surrounding the overtime coin toss that transpired during KC's 33-30 win over the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday night.
articles.body:
Kansas City Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce addressed the confusion surrounding the overtime coin toss that transpired during KC's 33-30 win over the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday night.

Speaking during Wednesday's episode of the New Heights podcast (beginning at the 23-minute mark) with his brother, former Philadelphia Eagles center Jason Kelce, Travis talked about Colts safety Camryn Bynum initially saying he wanted to "defer" after winning the OT toss.

"I don't even know if defer is something you can say in that situation," Travis said. "So by him saying, 'Defer,' the ref was like, 'That's not one of your options.'"

When Bynum said he wanted to defer, Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes attempted to jump on the situation by saying the Colts wanted to receive to start overtime.

Ultimately, referee Craig Wrolstad decided to talk it out with Bynum in order to get it right, and Bynum eventually said the Colts wanted to play defense first, meaning they wanted to kick the ball away.

Since both teams are allowed to possess the ball at least once in overtime unless there is a safety or time runs out during the first drive, it has become popular for teams to choose to kick rather than receive, as it allows them to know whether they need a touchdown or field goal on their offensive possession.

As the Kelce brothers highlighted, deferring is not an option on the OT coin toss, and it is only something a player can choose on the opening coin toss of the game.

Deferring in that situation means the team that wins the toss is saving their choice of whether they want to kick or receive for the second half. Naturally, the deferring team always picks to receive to open the second half.

Since there is no second half of overtime, there is nothing to defer to, which is why Bynum's initial choice on the OT coin flip was not valid.
